We do not buy today; we buy at or under about $206, or re-underwrite after the late-November Q3 FY27 print shows whether Communications backlog is still growing.

thesis.point: The driver build (approved set plus Kilian's middle backlog trim) gives a research target (12m) of $294.37, +33% from $221.05, on a multiple well below peers.
thesis.evidence: Horizon NTM P/E 13.2x (own 12.13x today vs 18.65x whole-company peer median of MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG) weighted 0.7 ($288.63) and LTM EV/EBITDA 10.2x on pro-forma own EBITDA weighted 0.3 ($307.76); the five independent forecasts, made before the trim, span $299.55-$315.37 (the trim takes -2.7% off the untrimmed $302.46). Build EPS FY27 ~18.3-18.5 vs Zacks 15.98 and StockAnalysis 17.06.

thesis.point: Demand is slowing, not breaking: Communications backlog is flat while carrier capex is trimmed, and BEAD and long-haul land mostly after the 12-month horizon.
thesis.evidence: DY NTM Communications backlog 5,376 (Q1 FY27) -> 5,362 (Q2 FY27), flat; the path now in the set (Kilian's middle trim, 2026-11-02 7:26 p.m. ET) needs 5,420 in Q3 and 5,580 in Q4 (was 5,450 / 5,650), then +1.75% a quarter in FY28 and +1.5% in FY29. AT&T cut 2027-28 capital investment to $22-23B a year from $23-24B but kept >60M fiber locations by 2030; Verizon held 2026 capex at $16-16.5B. MasTec Communications backlog fell 7.5% q/q (flat y/y) with customer deferrals. All 56 BEAD final proposals are approved; >270,000 route miles, ~58% buried, construction 'in earnest' in FY28.

thesis.point: Insiders bought near current levels and the company keeps beating its own guide, which supports the base case through the Q3 print.
thesis.evidence: Open-market purchases: CEO 850 shares at $296.76 (09-09), directors 700 at $286.92 (09-01) and 350 at $280.62 (09-23). Q3 FY27 guide adj. EPS $4.33-4.79; the build carries ~5.2, Street 4.33 (whisper 4.55, 80% range 4.24-4.88), after six straight EPS beats of the guide midpoint.

memo.variant_view: Two consensus views bracket us. Sell-side analysts (11, Strong Buy, median $525, mean $520.91, range $375-625, as of 10-09) are stale, set mostly May-September before the 61% fall from $566.47, and get zero weight in the target. The options market's 12-month distribution is the other pole: median $208.08 (below spot), 15th-85th range $111.42-$312.30, P(gain) 46%, with 1-year implied volatility ~60%. Our research leg (median $268.97, P(gain) 63.5%) is more constructive because the build follows DY's beat record and puts BEAD, long-haul and data-center work into the multiple; the published blend (67% market, 33% research) lands at $231.80. So the variant view is real on value (research target (12m) $294.37 vs options median $208) but not strong enough to clear the hurdle at today's price: the market is pricing a carrier capex slowdown (AT&T's 10-21 cut, MasTec's deferrals) that our path reflects only in part even after the middle trim Kilian chose on the supervisor's recommendation (four of five forecasters and the supervisor had called the original approved path full). Events past the 12-month horizon cut both ways and are weighed through the multiple: FTTH programs mature around 2030-32 (p 0.45, about -$12/sh), BEAD and long-haul extend Communications past the FTTH peak (p 0.5, about +$10/sh), a data-center construction turn in CY2028-29 (p 0.25, about -$10/sh), and carrier consolidation pricing (p 0.3, about -$6/sh); keeping ~29% of DY's discount to peers (exit k=0.8) is how the visible FTTH end date is priced.

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $294.37 = model engine on Kilian's quarterly driver set (Communications NTM backlog, conversion and margin; Building Systems share of US private data-center construction and margin), with the Communications backlog path set by his middle-trim decision: NTM P/E 13.2x ($288.63, weight 0.7) and LTM EV/EBITDA 10.2x on pro-forma own EBITDA ($307.76, weight 0.3), net debt 2,479.7 at 2026-08-01 rolled with FCF less $70M a year of buybacks, less 204.3 of debt-like supplier finance, ~30.0M shares at the horizon, SBC costed once. Downside case (P10) $135.05, upside case (P90) $457.63; thesis break $165. No DCF leg. Published 12-month target $231.80 = blend of the options-market leg ($208.08, 67%) and research leg ($268.97, 33%); expected (mean) $263.41 (+19.2%), P(gain) 53.1%. Entry below = $231.80 / 1.123 (T-bill + beta premium, no dividend) = about $206.42. Judgment calls: (1) Communications backlog after AT&T's capex cut: DECIDED by Kilian (decision card 2026-11-02 7:26 p.m. ET): middle trim (Q3 FY27 5,420, Q4 5,580, +1.75%/qtr FY28, +1.5%/qtr FY29; FY28 year-end 5,981.1, FY29 6,348.1), now in the set: $294.37 (-2.7% vs the approved path's $302.46; the agent_3 path would give $288.87). Still open with Kilian, valued on the pre-trim $302.46 base: (2) Supplier finance ($367.4M): debt-like part 204.3 on the payable-days test (recommended, in the set); none $309.27 (+2.3%); all 367.4 $297.03 (-1.8%). (3) DY's own trailing EV/EBITDA: pro-forma 9.44x (pre-close add ~69) -> exit 10.2x (recommended, in the set); as-filed 10.15x -> exit 10.8x $309.41. (4) Agent_4 variant: no (recommended; its backlog part overlaps the middle trim now taken); backlog part only $298.76; margin part only (-50bp from Q3 FY27) $290.25; both $286.73 (-5.2%). None of these changes the no-buy call: even the untrimmed build ($302.46) left the published target below the hurdle at $221.05.

Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.reasoning: Delta refresh of my 2026-10-02 file. I re-checked filings first. EDGAR shows no 8-K, 10-Q or proxy since Aug 10; the only new filing is an Oct 2 Form 4. So I re-opened and confirmed every reported figure that feeds my fair value at source: the Q2 8-K, the 10-Q, the Q2 call transcript, and the June 5 and Aug 10 8-Ks. The only company releases are the Oct 6 Constellation PPA (890 MW of uprates, 20 years; a separate 2,700 MW, 15-year supply deal; first uprate 2028; cost undisclosed) and the Sep 30/Oct 1 Gemini 4 Argon preview (Fairwind-only, no GA date). Neither changes a 12-month number. Neither does the stock's move: +1.2% Oct 2-6, in line with QQQ's +1.3%. What did change is consensus. CY2027 EPS is now $15.10 (S&P Global; 24/7 Wall St shows $14.47 to $15.10 in 90 days), against $14.84 in my last file. MarketScreener carries CY2028 at $17.89. I also built the 10-peer comp set my prior file lacked, on one CY2027 basis. Its median is 19.6x P/E and 11.9x EV/EBITDA; GOOGL is at 23.0x all-in and 22.0x core. I now apply 21x core, down from 21.5x and anchored to that peer set, to CY2028E EPS of $17.0 (consensus less about 5% for 2027-capex D&A, sized from the standing capex view: Big-4 2027 base +47%), up from $16.5. For one month, the Q3 print is about 97% inside the window, two-sided, centred at about $349. Lane: 9 of the 15 non-comp sources are primary (60%). agents.reasoning: Skeptic lane. Starting facts (filings): Q2-26 revenue $119.8B (+24%), operating income $40.8B, Cloud $24.8B (+82%) with $8.8B OI, Cloud backlog $513.9B [1][2]. What the consensus may be underweighting: (1) Earnings quality. H1-26 pretax income $216.2B includes $135.9B of equity-security gains (SpaceX IPO and other marks; $94.1B of SpaceX stock, mostly locked up [2][42]) [9][1], so trailing P/E of ~17x is misleading. On ex-gains consensus the stock is 23.2x CY27 [14]. (2) Cash. Q2 FCF -$5.9B, TTM $53.3B [1]. Consensus FCF is $8.4B in 2026 and -$36.7B in 2027 on capex of $201.7B and $301.0B [15], consistent with the standing AI-capex view (Alphabet 2027 consensus $285-357B) [40]. Purchase commitments jumped to $707B [3]. (3) Funding mix. Buybacks went from $13.2B in Q2-25 to zero [1]. Alphabet sold 58M Class A/C shares (net $20.5B) plus $10B to Berkshire, $19B of 6.25% mandatory convertibles, and set up a $40B ATM [4][5][6], plus $45B of bonds in Feb/Aug [7][8][39]. (4) Credit is pricing more risk. On like-for-like tenors, new-issue spreads widened from Feb to Aug: 10y T+63 -> T+85, 40y T+95 -> T+130, despite unchanged AA+/Aa2 ratings [7][8]. The Feb sterling deal included a 2126 century bond at gilts +120bp [41]. That is a mild, not alarming, signal. (5) Concentration and circularity. Anthropic reportedly accounts for over 40% of the backlog [31], and Google backstops financing of Anthropic's TPU purchases [32]. These are press reports (The Information, via Silicon UK), used here only to size bear-case probability, not as valuation inputs. (6) Sentiment is crowded: 0 sells and 4 holds out of 55 analysts; insiders sold ~$8.7M and bought $0 over 3 months [37]. Visible Form 4s are routine 10b5-1 or vesting [11][12][13], so this is not a red flag. Alt-data and markets: StatCounter puts Google at 89.94% of worldwide search in Sep-26 [35]. On Kalshi (via Octagon, Oct 2, week of Oct 5), 'Above 20.5%' Google share of OpenRouter text-model requests traded ~75% and 'Above 19.9%' 97%, with 30,430 contracts on the latter [36]. That reads as a solid but not dominant AI-model position. Privacy litigation remains a recurring cost (shareholder proponents cite a $425.7M privacy jury verdict [38]; PriceRunner $2.1B damages and the $5.2B EU Android payment in Q2-Q3 [3]). What weakens the bear case: the ad tech remedy decision rejected the AdX divestiture and imposed a 6-year behavioral decree [27][28][29][30], removing the largest structural legal tail. The balance sheet remains AA+. Operating momentum is real. Valuation: P/E (21.8x, between the all-peer median 19.8x and the US median 23.5x) on haircut NTM EPS gives $360. EV/EBITDA at the peer median (10.5x) gives $320. Blended fair value is $346, about 0.5% below spot. Scenarios: 257/348/440 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$348). The ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sigma 0.22/0.17/0.17), giving a log-sd of ~0.27 and median ~$348. This is somewhat tighter than the 32% realized vol, because the realized figure includes the Mar-May 2026 re-rating (weekly close $274 in late March to a $408.61 high in May) [43], and wider than base-rate large-cap moves only in the left tail. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate and statistics endpoints were plan-restricted, so consensus comes from MarketScreener and StockAnalysis. Seeking Alpha, Axios and some trade press were not fetchable.

memo.title: GOOGL: Long, small. 25% core EPS growth at 22x with the Anthropic/SpaceX stakes as a free option; target $371.53 (+8.4%)
memo.call_reason: The published target ($371.53) is above the $342.75 close, P(gain) is 0.59 and sizing conviction is medium, so this is a small, staged long. It is not a special situation.
memo.one_liner: Alphabet trades at about 21x forward core EPS while FY2027 consensus EPS grows about 25% with revisions running 8 up to 1 down, Cloud grows 82% on a $514B backlog, and roughly $13-15/sh of SpaceX/Anthropic stakes carry a November IPO option. The edge is modest (+8% to target against 36% implied vol), so we buy 2 shares in two tranches around the Q3 print and keep the stop at $256.52.

thesis.point: Earnings compound at a multiple that already prices in the capex debate.
thesis.evidence: FY2027 consensus core EPS is about $14.92 (+25%), with 8 upward and 1 downward revision in 30 days. NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the horizon, at about 22x, gives $356-372 before stakes. The ~$257B 2027 capex consensus is already in that multiple.

thesis.point: Cloud is now a second profit engine, not an option.
thesis.evidence: Q2 2026 Cloud revenue grew about 82% with a $514B backlog, and TPU system sales to third parties begin in 2027. Backlog conversion is what supports FY2027 numbers while Search decelerates.

thesis.point: The equity stakes and base rates add a right tail at little cost.
thesis.evidence: SpaceX is about $82B (551M shares at $148.68, $14.1B locked until Q3 2027) and Anthropic is carried at $124.3B on a $47.6B cost. A reported November IPO at about $2T would add roughly $5-11/sh after tax. Separately, 9 of 10 prior 15% drawdowns were higher a year later; the one exception required EPS to fall 19%.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view; this is a modest long. We sit between two consensuses. Our $371.53 target is well below the sell side (49 analysts, mean $425.45, median $425, range $310-515, Strong Buy), because we apply about 22x NTM core EPS and haircut for 2027 capex, negative FCF and the $84.75B equity program, which the Street's ~$425 largely looks through. We are slightly above the options market: its distribution centers on $358.96 with P(gain) 0.554 and a 15th percentile of $247.69, against our $371.53, P(gain) 0.593 and $256.52. Our small premium to the options market comes from the fact-checked EPS revision trend and the stake/IPO optionality. The difference is about 3.5% of price, which is not enough to call it a mispricing.

valuation.methods: Supervisor-reconciled research target (12m) of $367 (range across five agents $360-375). The main method is NTM core P/E: about 22x on NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the Sept 2027 horizon gives $356-372. Added to that are about $13-15/sh of after-tax stake value (SpaceX corrected to about $82B; Anthropic at its $124.3B carrying value) plus about $4-5/sh of probability-weighted Anthropic IPO uplift. A rolled-forward SOTP (about $370) is the cross-check. DCF cross-checks at $313-340 reflect the ~$257B 2027 capex consensus and are weighted about 20%. The published target of $371.53 is the median of the blended options/forecaster distribution, weighted 67% market and 33% forecasters; the expected value is $391.56 (+14.2%).

catalysts.event: Joint proposed Final Judgment due in the DOJ ad-tech case (court-ordered 30-day deadline after Judge Brinkema's Sept 2 remedies ruling; no AdX divestiture)
catalysts.why_it_moves: It locks in behavioral-only remedies (Prebid interoperability, bid-data sharing, a 6-year monitor) and removes the breakup tail. Most of this is already priced after Sept 2.
catalysts.watch: Disputed provisions submitted separately, the scope of the worldwide AdX rival-access terms, and Google's notice of appeal.

catalysts.date: Oct-Dec 2026 (Google says 'much earlier' than year-end; October rumored)
catalysts.event: Gemini 4 release (replaces the delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first test of model leadership after DeepMind talent departures and the Meta Muse launch. A strong launch would ease the 'Search gets disintermediated' fear; a slip or weak benchmarks would feed it.
catalysts.watch: Release date versus the October chatter, head-to-head benchmarks against OpenAI/Anthropic/Meta models, and Gemini app MAU and AI Mode usage disclosed alongside it.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings. Consensus core EPS is about $3.02 and revenue about $127B. Alphabet IR has not yet announced the call date.
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first print since Meta Muse and the $84.75B raise, and the first official color on 2027 capex. Q2 showed that a capex surprise alone can move the stock down on a beat.
catalysts.watch: Search & other growth against Q2's +17% (single digits would signal a thesis break), paid-click trends, Cloud growth and the $514B backlog, any early 2027 capex framing against the ~$257B consensus, FCF after Q2's -$5.9B, ATM usage beyond sell-to-cover, and the GAAP SpaceX mark-to-market loss (excluded from core EPS).

catalysts.event: Meta Q3 2026 earnings: first quantified read on Muse agent engagement
catalysts.why_it_moves: Muse was the trigger for GOOGL's 3% drop on Sept 23. Strong Muse usage or commerce-query data would reinforce the Search-disintermediation narrative, while weak adoption would ease it.
catalysts.watch: Muse DAU/MAU, agentic shopping or query volume, and Meta's 2027 capex guide (a read-across on AI capex tolerance).

catalysts.event: Anthropic IPO at a reported ~$2T valuation, raising up to ~$100B
catalysts.why_it_moves: The IPO would re-mark Alphabet's stake, now carried at $124.3B on a $47.6B cost, and disclose the ownership percentage (estimated at 10-15%). That is about +$5-11/sh after tax at $2T. A slip or a lower price would remove part of the right tail.
catalysts.watch: A public S-1 flip (it typically comes about 15 days before the roadshow), Alphabet's disclosed ownership, the pricing range against $2T, and first-day trading.

catalysts.date: Oct 9, Oct 24 and Dec 8, 2026 (remaining SPCX insider lock-up tranches; Dec 8 is the final 180-day release)
catalysts.event: SpaceX lock-up tranche expiries
catalysts.why_it_moves: Alphabet's ~551M SPCX shares (about $82B) move with SPCX. A 20% SPCX drop costs roughly $1.3/sh pre-tax, so this is a stake-value nuisance, not a thesis driver.
catalysts.watch: SPCX price reaction around each tranche. Alphabet's $14.1B long-term restricted block stays locked until Q3 2027.

catalysts.date: Q4 2026 - Q1 2027 (oral argument not yet scheduled; Google's reply brief due Sept 29)
catalysts.event: DC Circuit oral argument in the search monopoly appeal (Google appeals liability and remedies; DOJ cross-appeals for a default-payment ban and Chrome divestiture)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The argument itself only moves sentiment through the panel's questions. The ruling, likely mid-2027 or later, sets whether the Apple default payments and Chrome are at risk.
catalysts.watch: The scheduling order, panel composition, and the panel's questions on the payment ban and Chrome.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 earnings with the formal 2027 capex guide
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the single biggest swing factor. The FactSet consensus is about $257B (Evercore $262B). A guide far above that, with FCF negative into 2028 and more equity issuance, is the main path to the $250 thesis break. A guide at or below consensus paired with visible Cloud returns would re-rate the stock.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex against $257B, depreciation guide, FCF trajectory, whether buybacks resume, and Cloud operating margin.

risks.risk: Agentic assistants (Meta Muse, ChatGPT) take commercial queries, and Search growth falls from +17% to single digits, causing an actual EPS downgrade rather than multiple noise.
risks.signpost: Search & other growth below ~10% in the Q3 or Q4 print, decelerating paid clicks, strong Muse engagement numbers from Meta on Oct 28, and FY2027 EPS revisions turning net negative.

risks.risk: The capex/FCF spiral: the 2027 guide lands well above ~$257B, depreciation compresses margins, FCF stays negative and the $40B ATM or more equity dilutes beyond sell-to-cover.
risks.signpost: Q3 commentary pre-guiding 2027 capex well above $257B, another negative-FCF quarter, and ATM issuance well above RSU tax-withholding levels in the 10-Q.

risks.risk: An AI-valuation reset removes the stake credit: the Anthropic IPO slips or prices well below $2T, and SPCX keeps falling.
risks.signpost: No public S-1 by early November, a price range well below $2T, or SPCX breaking below about $120 (from $148.68).

risks.risk: Model competitiveness slips (Gemini 4 delay, DeepMind talent losses), undermining both Search defense and Cloud/TPU demand.
risks.signpost: Gemini 4 slipping into 2027 or trailing rival models on launch benchmarks, and further senior DeepMind departures.

trade.position: 2 sh (~$686, 6.9% of the $10,000 book); supervisor cap 12%. Size was set by the joint portfolio solve (overlap with AVGO, META and SPY), not by the stop budget.
trade.entry: Two tranches per the supervisor: buy 1 share now near $342.75 and 1 share after the Q3 2026 report (expected Oct 27). The second tranche goes in only if FY2027 core EPS revisions stay positive and there is no capex pre-guide far above the ~$257B consensus. A close below $250 cancels it.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit at the $256.52 stop (15th percentile), and in any case on a close below the $250 thesis break, which is about 17x FY2027 EPS with no stake credit. Take profit at $465.33. Add up to the 12% cap if Q3 shows Search at 12% or higher with Cloud backlog growing, or if the Feb 2027 capex guide is at or below about $257B with a credible FCF path. Also exit if the capex guide comes in far above consensus with FCF guided negative through 2028. [Updated 2026-11-13: the one upside exit is now $370.89, where the 12-month expected value no longer beats the 4% cash sleeve and the model sells every share; any other take-profit figure in this memo is superseded.]
trade.take_profit_note: expected value: the price where the 12-month expected return (research fixed in dollars, options leg moving with the price) falls to the 4% cash rate (full exit) (as of 2026-11-13)

what_changes_our_mind: Search & other growth prints in single digits in Q3 or Q4 2026 while FY2027 EPS revisions turn net negative (the 2022 pattern). That would be a thesis break, and we would exit.
A February 2027 capex guide well above ~$257B (for example $280B+) with FCF negative into 2028 and further equity issuance. We would cut the position.

Upside case: Anthropic prices at or above $2T in November, Alphabet discloses 14% or more ownership, and Q3 shows Cloud backlog above $514B with stable margins. We would add to the 12% cap and raise the research target (12m).

Net effect on fair value: removing the phantom dilution helps, while the NCI, the higher H2 net debt and the escrow shares hurt, so fair value goes from $99 to $96. Starting point is unchanged: INTC is $120 after +258% in a year and +34% in September, at about 58x FY27 consensus EPS of $2.06 and about 11x sales, near the top of its decade P/S range [1][2][4][5]. Base rates (own computation, 28 large semis/tech names [17]): after a +150% trailing year the median next-12-month return was +48% (n=243), or +25% for the post-2002 ex-mega-winner subset (n=72), with a log SD of 0.63-0.82 and about 19% of cases losing more than 30%. Survivorship bias is heavy, so I cut the momentum drift to about 0-10%. Valuation pulls the other way: fair value of about $96 is 20% below spot, and Intel's 2000 peak at about 50x was followed by -82% [19]. Sell-side consensus of about $116, with 32 of 48 at Hold [1][10], agrees with a flat-to-down center. Manifold's 41% on touching $150 by end-2026 [15] is a bit below a driftless touch model (~55%). Per the source review, I now give no weight to the thin 2027 Polymarket markets (~$10k volume) [11][13]. That removes a little of the bear tail I had attributed to macro. Removing the supply overhang of a phantom follow-on is a small positive for the 12-month path. Together these move my median from $112 to $113. I keep sigma at 0.65 (between the base-rate sample's 0.63-0.82 and slightly below the 76% realized vol, since vol mean-reverts after spikes). Result: P(>=120) is 46%, P(>=60) is 84%, and P(>=300) is 7%. The scenario mean (0.25x$60 + 0.5x$110 + 0.25x$185 = $116) is consistent. I agree with the supervisor's factual corrections. I keep my own ladder rather than the forecaster mean because my base-rate evidence still argues for fatter tails on both sides. Research limits: round-1 data constraints (Twelve Data paywall, Alpha Vantage rate limit) still apply, and round 2 used 7 targeted fetches (EDGAR, 424B5, 8-K, Intel IR).

agents.reasoning: Round 2 update. The supervisor's fact-checks, which I verified, moved my inputs up modestly. (1) FY28 consensus EPS is $4.58 on $7.43B revenue (Alpha Vantage, 25 analysts, up from $4.19 60 days ago, 20 up / 1 down revisions in 30 days); my round-1 $6.8B revenue was below the lowest estimate ($6.985B), so I rebuilt FY28 at ~$7.3B. (2) Non-GAAP tax is ~7.5%, which with 65% GM and ~40% op margin gives ~$4.41 FY28 on 575M shares; I set NTM EPS at the horizon at ~$4.50 (up from $4.40), still below the consensus roll-forward as cycle discipline. (3) Net debt was $5.09B in June and falls ~$250-300M/qtr after dividends, so ~$3.8B by Sep-2027 (vs my $4.0B). (4) At Citi (2026-09-09) the CFO guided GM roughly flat at 66-67% into December, called distributor inventory low at 25 days and said there is no evidence of significant customer stocking; internal lead times are steady, and the stretch is at outsourced capacity. I did not raise the multiple: the 10-yr UST at ~5.14% and the sector derating keep me at 19x, and I trimmed the EV/EBITDA multiple to 15.5x. This is below the supervisor's $85 because I haircut EPS a bit more (bottom-up ~$4.41 vs consensus $4.58) and use EV-based rather than equity FCF yield. Scenarios: bear $52 (20%), base $87 (55%), bull $125 (25%), probability-weighted ~$89 before a ~2.3% dividend. Ladder: a mixture of lognormals, 83% median $86 with sigma 0.39 and 17% median $66 with sigma 0.58. This keeps a fat left tail consistent with 50% realized vol and semis cyclicality. The ladder median is ~$83.3 (from ~$81), P(>=79) is 0.55 and P(>=106) is 0.28. Analyst mean PT ~$100 is evidence of sell-side optimism, not an anchor. thesis.evidence: At $74.16 the stock trades at 16.2x FY28 consensus (74.16 / 4.58) and ~18.0x NTM (estimate: 74.16 / (0.5 x 3.65 + 0.5 x 4.58)). Net debt was $5,089M at Jun-2026 (5,361.3 debt - 272.3 cash), or 2.85x adjusted TTM EBITDA. Management keeps the dividend flat (45.5c/qtr, 2.45% yield = 1.82 / 74.16) and plans no buybacks until the balance sheet improves. Upside is +6.4% to the target and +14.6% to the research target (12m), against -25.8% to the $55 thesis break.

memo.variant_view: There is no real variant view versus the Street on direction; our view differs on the multiple, and the Street is well above us. Our weighted set of 22 analyst targets (as of 2026-10-13, from MarketBeat; consensus rating Buy) has a weighted median of $95, a weighted mean of $102.04 and a range of $69-125. That implies 20.7x and 22.3x FY28 consensus (95 / 4.58; 102.04 / 4.58). The S&P Global consensus on StockAnalysis is higher still: 26 analysts, average $107.84, median $108, range $80-135 (2026-10-14). Our forecasters use 18.5-19x NTM, because at the Oct-2027 horizon the market will be pricing FY29 on a mature upcycle, with the 10-yr Treasury at 5.21% (2026-10-13). The options market on its own is less constructive than we are: median $71.93, P(gain) 0.48, 15th percentile $42.98. Our forecasters on their own are more constructive: median $92.56, P(gain) 0.70. The published blend (0.67 market, 0.33 forecasters) gives a $78.92 median and P(gain) 0.55. Our edge over the options market is about 7 points of P(gain) (0.55 vs 0.48) and rests on the lean channel and the flat-GM guide, which is too little to override the book's exclusion.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $85 (supervisor; agents $83-86, mean $84.3) blends three methods. (1) P/E, weight 0.5: 18.75x x ~$4.60 NTM EPS at Sep-2027 = $86.25 (estimate; consensus FY28 $4.58 rolled forward, less a light cycle haircut; 575M non-GAAP diluted shares). (2) FCF yield, weight 0.3, equity basis: ~$2.45-2.6B FY28 FCF at a 5.0-5.2% required yield = $85.2-87.0 (2.45 / 0.05 / 0.575; 2.6 / 0.052 / 0.575; FCF ~33% of ~$7.4B sales, Q1 FY27 FCF margin 33.5%). (3) EV/EBITDA, weight 0.2: (16 x ~$3.2B - ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt) / 0.575 = $82.4. The supervisor harmonized this leg to 16x from agents 1-4's 14-15.5x (agent 5 already used 16x), which double-counted the derating. Blend: 0.5 x 86.25 + 0.3 x 86 + 0.2 x 82.4 = $85.4, rounded to $85. Scenarios: bear $52 (20-22%), base $86-88 (53-55%), bull $118-125 (25%). Published 12-month distribution (2026-10-13): median (target) $78.92, mean $87.87 (+18.5%), 25th/75th percentile $56.46/$108.81. The ~2.45% dividend is on top. The research passed the citation gate on 2026-10-14 (clean: 78 checked, 11 fixed); no fix changed a number. TRIAL STANDARD MODEL, shown beside the published target and not the target: a standard model built on 2026-10-14 from the same research gives a model target of $85.40 at the research date's $78.69 spot (+8.5%; +15.2% against today's $74.16, derived 85.40 / 74.16), and research target (12m) $85.32 = 0.5 x $86.25 (P/E 18.75x on $4.60 NTM EPS) + 0.3 x $85.20 (5.0% FCF yield on $4.26/share) + 0.2 x $83.19 (16x EV/EBITDA). Bear/base/bull are $51.71/$85.32/$119.43 at 20/55/25%. Caveat: the 18.75x P/E sits at the top of, slightly above, the ~13.7-18.5x NTM P/E range of NXPI and ON (rebuilt by the citation gate from 2026-09-25 closes and StockAnalysis consensus EPS, time-weighted NTM), so the model leans on the high end of peer multiples. The published target remains $78.92.

agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it gets in the Jan-2027 dividend; 8-K 2026-10-21); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Evidence, mostly primary: Q3-26 release, 10-Q and call; Q2-26 call; nine prior releases for the guidance record. The core is strong: revenue +26% (impressions +10%, price +14%), Q4 guide $73-76B (+22-27%), and Meta beat the top of its range in 6 of 8 quarters. The debate is cost: FY26 expenses $175-179B (incl. $12.3B legal), capex $135-145B, $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments ($121.4B due 2027), management 'investing aggressively' in 2027, and RL loss ~$15B. Driver build: FY27 revenue $312B (at consensus) from impressions +9% and price +10% plus new AI revenue; FoA margin 51.6% FY25 -> 37.8% FY27 -> 34.5% FY28 as D&A rises with capex that follows the AI capex file ($192B, $236B; above street). FY27 EPS ~$32 (~5% below consensus $33.9). Valuation: SOTP $750 (FoA 16.5x NTM EBIT, RL -$25B), P/E 20x $691, EV/EBITDA 10x $681 -> research target (12m) $715.83, +11% vs $642.62. Scenarios: bear $409 (25%), base $716 (50%), bull $1,019 (25%). Ladder: 75% this scenario mix (within-scenario vol 17-18%) plus 25% a market-anchored lognormal (median $650, sigma 33%, about the stock's 43% realized vol trimmed for non-earnings periods), since price is the best single forecast. That gives a median of ~$697 and P(>= $643) = 0.59. Not driver-linked: the RL venture value (-$25B), the litigation and investment adjustments, and RL revenue. Research limits: the Q3 call transcript was reached at a content_files URL; no option data was used.

agents.reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it receives on 2027-01-19); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Industry lane: the rest of the ad chain says demand is still strong but slowing. WARC's Q3-26 outlook has social ad spend +21.3% in 2026 and +14.6% in 2027, total +11.9% then +8.4% [13]; IAB US social +16.5% in 2026 [14]; Google Search +17%, YouTube +13%, Amazon ads +26%, Reddit ads +64%, Pinterest +18%, Snap ads only +9% in Q2-26 [16-20]; eMarketer puts Meta's 2026 ad revenue at ~$242B [30]. Meta's own impressions growth fell from +19% (Q1) to +10% (Q3) while price per ad rose to +14% [6][5][1]; an agency newsletter reports large CPM rises [31] (lead only, low weight). On the cost side the supply chain says Meta's bill keeps rising: CoreWeave $21B through 2032 [21], Nebius $12B from early 2027 [22], DRAM contract prices still rising [23], neocloud rental pricing up >50% YTD (MS proprietary index, used only as direction) [25], $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments and $355.7B of leases not yet commenced [2]. So the driver build has FY2027 revenue +17.7% (impressions +8%, price +9%), 2.4% under consensus, and FoA margin falling to 37.4% as D&A rises to $47B; FY2027 EPS ~$31 vs $33.92 consensus. Capex follows the AI-capex file base ($141B in 2026, $192B in 2027) [24]. Guidance record: five straight quarterly revenue guides at or above the range (median +3.4% vs midpoint), expense guides inside, capex guides overshot in 2024-25. Valuation: SOTP (FoA 16x EV/EBIT, RL separately at -$94B), P/E 19x and EV/EBITDA 10.5x give a research target (12m) of $691 after -$19.9B accrued legal and -$10.5B probability-weighted litigation. Ladder: bear $455 / base $680 / bull $920 at 25/50/25 with 25% within-scenario vol (total ~35% log vol vs 43% realized); the centre (~$670 median) sits between the price and the research target because the price is the better one-year predictor. No option data used. Research limited: Q3-26 peer results (Alphabet, Snap, Pinterest, Reddit) are not out yet; X/Twitter not used; no prediction market found on a Meta event that matters (Kalshi lists only headcount contracts). In-lane sources: 19 of 31.

DC margin: 14.8% in Q1 (Ex.99.1); management expects the DC margin back at 19-20% in Q2 (CFO Mick Lucareli, Q1 FY27 call (company transcript): "When we look at going into Q2, we would expect, right now, a lift to be back between 19% and 20%, really driven by a significant lift in the volume recovering." src 38); I assume ~19% for the year (judgment). That is deliberately BELOW the explicit Q1-slide guide of DC 'full-year earnings growth in excess of 85%' (>= $397M, which needs ~23% margins in Q2-Q4 after Q1's $51.7M). HVAC margin 16.5% (16.7% in FY26). Corporate -$80M: Q1 FY27 adjusted corporate & eliminations was -$23.0M (vs -$15.5M a year earlier), ~-$92M annualised, against -$62.6M in FY26. I take a bit less than the run-rate because TSA fees from PT offset some of it. Q1 RemainCo EBITDA was $70.3M ($51.7M + $41.6M - $23.0M), so Q2-Q4 need ~$375M.

Management's Jan-2026 target is DC +50-70% a year for two years. I use +45%, below the range, for supply/execution risk and a possible capex digestion; that matches the capex note's base case of 2027 customer AI capex +50%. DC margin 20% (judgment; FY26 reported 19.4%). HVAC +6%. Corporate -$82M, up from -$80M on inflation, per the Q1 run-rate.
DC growth decelerates to +20% as AI capex growth slows (the capex note's base case has 2028 customer capex +22%).

That gives a median of 20.73x (range 11.3-29.46x). The EPS-CAGR divisor gives 19.74x and the average divisor 20.23x, so I treat ~20x as the reference. 16.5x is inside the range, ~18% below ~20x. The discount rests on structural features that persist through Oct-2027: (a) concentration, with one technology customer ~11% of consolidated FY26 sales per the 10-K, ~30% of DC sales if all of it is Data Centers (estimate: 0.11 x $3,181.1M FY26 sales / $1,108.2M DC sales = ~32%; the 10-K places the customer only in the Climate Solutions segment); (b) about 30% of NTM EBITDA is commercial HVAC, whose peers LII/CARR/SPXC sit at 11.3-17.9x (derived); (c) DC EBITDA margins of ~19-20% vs VRT's ~22% (TTM GAAP EBITDA $2,561.8M / revenue $11,479.6M to 2026-06-30, 10-Q XBRL); (d) the NTM window at Oct-2027 includes DC growth decelerating to ~+20% in FY29. agents.reasoning: I valued only the remaining Climate Solutions company from recast segment data in Modine's filings: FY26 Data Centers $1.11B sales / $214.7M EBITDA, Commercial HVAC $974M / $162.4M. FY27 guidance is DC +60-80% and HVAC +5-10%. The Q1 slides also promise DC 'full-year earnings growth in excess of 85%', and the Jan-2026 deck targets DC +50-70% a year for two years. Round 2 changes after re-checking the supervisor's points in the filings. (1) Corporate cost: the Q1 FY27 release shows adjusted corporate & eliminations of -$23.0M for the quarter (vs -$15.5M a year earlier), so I raise it from -$55M to -$80M a year. That cuts FY27E RemainCo EBITDA to ~$445M (Q1 actual $70.3M) and FY28E to ~$635M. (2) Net debt: I confirmed $432.9M at Jun 30 less the ~$156M distribution = ~$277M, i.e. ~$280M, as in round 1. (3) Comps: I dropped HUBB and the +3pt margin allowance and recomputed all 10 peers on TTM/(1+3Y revenue CAGR): median 20.5x, or ~19x reconciled with the EPS-divisor result. 16.5x is now a ~13% discount, justified by 10-K concentration (one customer ~11% of consolidated sales; ~30% of DC if all DC, an estimate), the HVAC mix and DC margins below VRT. (4) Calendar: the Nov 18 Analyst & Investor Day is confirmed and sits outside the 1-month window. The Q2 date is still unannounced but very likely ~Oct 26-29. On NTM Oct-2027 EBITDA of $700M at 16.5x and EPS of $8.54 at 24x, fair value is ~$208 (+14%), down from $215; most of the upside is earnings growth, not re-rating. I am still explicitly below management's DC earnings guide because Q1 margins make the >85% promise require ~23% margins for the rest of the year. Scenarios: bear $110 (25%), base $205 (50%), bull $305 (25%). memo.title: MOD: stay long but small (3 sh): a sector sell-off has taken the stock to $135, ~8% above our $125 thesis break, 12 days before the Nov 3 Q2 print, the expected first standalone guide
memo.call_reason: The published target of $161.51 is 19.5% above the $135.17 close and the research target (12m) is $200, but supervisor confidence is low and the review trims to the Sharpe-optimal size (4 to 3 sh) [1][2][3][9].
memo.one_liner: Modine is now a pure data-center and commercial HVAC cooling company that guides data-center sales +60-80% this year and has a $4B 2027-29 capacity agreement, yet it trades at $135.17, down 26% from the $182.91 research price of Oct 5, and the latest 9.75% drop came with no company news [3][9][10][17][18][19]. We keep a small long (target $161.51, research target (12m) $200) into the Nov 3 print and Nov 18 Investor Day, with a $125 thesis break and an $89.26 stop [1][3][13][14].

thesis.point: Data-center growth is guided and partly contracted, not just hoped for.
thesis.evidence: FY26 Data Centers sales were $1,108.2M with $214.7M adj. EBITDA (19.4%); the Q1 FY27 slides guide DC sales +60-80% and DC earnings growth >85% for FY27; the 10-K expects more than $4B of DC cooling sales to one customer in CY2027-29 (~$1.3B/yr); management's medium-term DC target is 50-70%/yr.

thesis.point: Margin recovery is the near-term lever, and the Nov 3 print tests it.
thesis.evidence: Q1 FY27 DC margin fell to 14.8% on $348.6M sales because of supply shortages; hitting the >85% DC earnings guide needs ~23% DC margins in Q2-Q4. No continuing-ops guide has been issued since the Oct 1 spin; the Q1 release said the outlook would be updated after the spin closed, and the supervisor expects it with the Q2 results due after the close on Nov 3.

thesis.point: The price already discounts a lot: at $135.17 the EV is ~$7.5B, ~13.4-13.9x NTM RemainCo EBITDA vs a 20.2x filing-derived peer median.
thesis.evidence: 53,196,918 shares x $135.17 + $265.3M pro forma net debt at June 30 (8-K/A Ex.99.1 of Oct 7: $43.4M current + $276.0M long-term debt - $54.1M cash; derived) = ~$7.46B EV over ~$535-555M NTM EBITDA (supervisor estimate). The Oct 22 drop (-9.75%, from $149.78) came with no Modine filing or release; Vertiv fell ~8% and GE Vernova ~11% the same day after Meta's Q3 release, which narrowed 2026 capex upward to $135-145B but showed -$2.12B Q3 free cash flow.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Analysts (9, Strong Buy) have a median target of $301 (low $260) on StockAnalysis, and our recency-weighted median of the individual targets is $293.67 (as of Oct 20); several were set before the Oct 1 spin and on premium multiples; our research target (12m) of $200 uses 17x EBITDA, a ~16% discount to peers justified by ~11% single-customer concentration and below-peer DC margins [1][3][18][22]. The options market's own 12-month median is $134.66, roughly today's price (it gives a 44% chance of closing above the Oct 21 mark of $149.78 and ~50% above today's $135.17); our research is more constructive because DC growth is guided and contracted [1][17][19]. The published target $161.51 weights the options market 67% and research 33% [1]. The variant is modest: we are not calling the Street's $290s, only that the stock is pricing an AI-capex down-cycle that the latest hyperscaler data (Meta raising the low end of 2026 capex) does not show [1][11].

Agent research targets (12m) $175-212 (four of five at $198-212); probability-weighted scenarios bear $105-125 / base $180-212 / bull $280-315 at 25/50/25. Through-cycle P/E 24x = peer lower quartile (NVDA 16.5, AVGO 20.8, COHR 24.3, CRDO 25.8; median of the four 22.6x, rounded up for MRVL growth). Weight 0.3 (playbook 0.2-0.4; judgment, untested). memo.title: NFLX: small two-step long in a de-rated cash compounder at ~18x 2027 EPS; the Oct 20 print and the January 2027 guide settle the engagement debate
memo.call_reason: The published 12-month target of $75.49 is 8.5% above the $69.58 close and the research target (12m) of $80.00 is 15.0% above it, at medium conviction; size is capped by the supervisor at ~8% because the engagement debate is unresolved and earnings are three weeks out.
memo.one_liner: Netflix has de-rated to ~18x 2027 consensus EPS on an engagement scare that has not yet reached churn (2% vs a 4% industry average) or pricing, while recurring FCF of ~$11.3-11.7B and a ~3-4% annual share shrink keep compounding per-share value. We buy 11 shares in two tranches around the Oct 20 print, target $75.49 / research target (12m) $80, take profit $97.77, stop at the $51 thesis break.

thesis.point: 1. Per-share cash compounding is intact and is being bought back cheaply.
thesis.evidence: Recurring 2026 FCF is ~$11.3-11.7B (the $11B pre-fee guide incl. the ~$700M Brazil deposit, vs $12.5B including the after-tax WBD fee), implying ~$13.0-13.5B in 2027. Net debt is only $5.24B (A2/A), and Q2 buybacks retired 52.9M shares, shrinking the 4.164B count ~3-4% a year.

thesis.point: 2. Monetisation shows no damage from the engagement debate yet.
thesis.evidence: Antenna July churn is 2% vs a 4% average for major services; the 2026 upfront nearly doubled ad commitments and the ad tier passed 250M monthly active viewers, with ads ~$3B in 2026. The fall season (~40% of annual gross adds) is the next test.

thesis.point: 3. The multiple already discounts a lot; the bar for the print is low.
thesis.evidence: At $69.58 the stock trades ~18x 2027 consensus EPS of $3.82 with 2028 at $4.56, near Wells Fargo's 15x bear multiple ($57 PT) after Wells Fargo and HSBC downgrades in September. Our research target (12m) of $80 needs only ~19x NTM EPS of ~$4.25 and a 4.5% FCF yield, not a return to the old 30x+.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the two consensus views. The options market's distribution (result.json market_only) is centred at $70.19 with P(gain) 0.51, i.e. it prices no edge; we have $75.49 and P(gain) 0.58 because the forecasters see churn, ad growth and buybacks absorbing the engagement drag. The sell-side is far more bullish (weighted median PT $95, Deutsche Bank upgrade to Buy at $95 on 9/29, Wells Fargo $57 underweight); we stay well below it because peer de-ratings of quality large caps (DIS, PYPL, NKE, ADBE) have a median ~-6% follow-through over the next 12 months, so we do not underwrite a re-rating before the January 2027 guide. The real variant view is modest: the market is treating an engagement metric (Nielsen 7.8% share vs YouTube 14.2%; Wells Fargo ~-4% y/y hours per member in H2'26) as if it were already a revenue problem.

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $80 (five forecasters $77-83, mean $80.3) = 60/40 blend of (a) P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of 0.25x$3.82 + 0.75x$4.56 = $4.38, less ~3% engagement haircut = $4.25, at 19x = ~$81; and (b) FCF: NTM FCF ~$14.5B at a 4.5% yield, less $5.24B net debt, over ~4.08B diluted shares = ~$77.7. The published 12-month target ($75.49, the median of the blended market/forecaster distribution) sits below the research target (12m) because the options market centres near spot; take profit $97.77 is the 75th percentile, stop $51 is the thesis break (~13.4x 2027 EPS, ~6.6% FCF yield).

catalysts.event: Paramount Skydance closes its WBD acquisition (all regulatory conditions met in Aug; 12-state AG settlement Sep 21)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Creates a combined HBO Max/Paramount+ rival with ~$80B of debt; integration plans and bundling/pricing signal how hard it will compete for subscribers and content.
catalysts.watch: Streaming bundle/pricing announcements, content-spend guidance and leverage of the combined company.

catalysts.event: First Nielsen Gauge on the recalibrated methodology (ARF DASH universe), covering the start of the fall TV season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Nielsen share (7.8% vs YouTube 14.2% in July) is the core of the bear case; a further drop under the new method would be read as confirmation even though it is a methodology break.
catalysts.watch: Netflix share of TV time vs the July 7.8% and YouTube's lead; any restatement of history under the new method.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide (letter 1:01pm PT, video interview 1:45pm PT)
catalysts.why_it_moves: First print since the September downgrades; the Q4 guide and any 2027 framing set the growth path the multiple hangs on. Q2's slight beat with a lower outlook sent the stock down after hours.
catalysts.watch: Revenue vs $12.86B guide, 33.2% operating margin, EPS $0.82; Q4 guide vs the $51.2B / 31.5% FY26 plan; engagement and ad-revenue commentary; Q3 buyback pace and FCF vs the ~$12.5B FY guide; early 2027 growth/margin framing (~10% growth, 33-34% margin needed).

catalysts.event: Antenna churn and sign-up reads through the fall acquisition season
catalysts.why_it_moves: Churn at 2% is the evidence that engagement loss has not reached monetisation; Sep-Dec is ~40% of annual gross adds, so a rise here would validate the bear case.
catalysts.watch: Netflix monthly churn above ~2.5%; gross adds vs prior years; ad-tier mix.

catalysts.event: NFL Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix (Packers at Rams), first of its kind
catalysts.why_it_moves: Live-sports tentpoles drive sign-ups and ad inventory and counter the engagement narrative; a streaming failure would hurt.
catalysts.watch: Reported viewership, stream stability, ad sell-out.

catalysts.event: Fury vs. Joshua heavyweight fight streamed live on Netflix (reported by trade/fan press, not yet verified in a company release)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A global live event at no extra cost; another engagement and sign-up spike for Q4.
catalysts.watch: Concurrent viewers; Q4 net-add commentary in January.

catalysts.event: NFL Christmas Day doubleheader exclusively on Netflix
catalysts.why_it_moves: Highest-profile ad inventory of the year; supports the ad-scaling leg of the thesis.
catalysts.watch: Viewership vs 2025 Christmas games; advertiser demand.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results and first full-year 2027 revenue, margin and FCF guidance
catalysts.why_it_moves: The main re-rating or de-rating event: ~10% 2027 growth with 33-34% margin supports the $80 research target (12m); high-single-digit growth or a flat margin is the bear path toward the $51 thesis break.
catalysts.watch: 2027 revenue growth vs ~10%, operating margin vs 33-34%, 2027 FCF vs ~$13.0-13.5B, buyback size, ad-revenue target.

catalysts.event: H2 2026 'What We Watched' engagement report
catalysts.why_it_moves: Direct test of Wells Fargo's ~-4% y/y hours-per-member call for H2'26.
catalysts.watch: Total hours and hours per member y/y; share of views from top titles.

risks.risk: Engagement erosion reaches churn and pricing power (YouTube and creators taking TV time).
risks.signpost: Antenna churn above ~2.5% for two consecutive months, Netflix share falling further on the recalibrated Gauge, or a weaker take-rate on the next price increase.

risks.risk: The January 2027 guide shows high-single-digit growth and a stalled margin, cutting 2027/28 EPS.
risks.signpost: A Q4 guide on Oct 20 below the implied $51.2B FY26 plan, or 2027 framing under ~10% growth / ~33% margin.

risks.risk: The de-rating persists even if fundamentals hold (peer base rate: median ~-6% follow-through in 12 months).
risks.signpost: Stock fails to rally on a clean Oct 20 print and stays below ~$63 into January.

tax_assumptions._ignore_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: ignore taxes for now (he has money set aside for the liability). Set false to use the tax facts below.
tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.reasoning: Base rates first. NVDA's own 12-month forward returns since 2002: median +40%, P(down) 22%, P(<-40%) 7%; in setups like today (prior year +10-45%, at a 52-week high, n=25) median +29%. That record is survivorship-biased for a $5.7T leader; the top-dog base rate (Arnott/Wu: largest companies trail their sector by ~4%/yr) and a ~7% market return pull the centre to roughly +5-12%. Round-2 corrections from the supervisor, all accepted: (1) my horizon NTM EPS used a window shifted one quarter forward; on the same Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 window as today's 19.3-19.7x it is ~$16.7 after a 5% haircut (also FY29 growth trimmed to +15% given consensus 2027 capex growth of only ~+22%, src 27); (2) my fair value used 18x while my base scenario used 15x; I now use one multiple, 16x, in both; (3) FCF conversion of 85% is not supported (Q2 FY27 FCF 36-39% of NI, H1 ~70%), now 75%, with ~$1/share true net cash; (4) the 10Y at 5.24-5.28% is verified at Treasury (src 26) but it is the highest since 2007, not 2002; (5) the Fed-odds source was misattributed; the Dec-9 meeting-specific Kalshi contract shows ~70% for a 25bp hike (search-result snapshot; direct fetch 429) and DeFi Rate 72%, so the macro headwind stands; (6) I dropped the 'historical 17-20x floor' argument. On compression: it has been estimate-driven (FY28 EPS +24% in 90 days while the price rose), so it is real but has not hurt holders; I assume 3.5 more turns (to 16x), while a flat year needs ~14.2x on my EPS, a de-rating that likely needs an EPS break. Fair value $255 (P/E $267, FCF $230, mid-cycle $260) is below my round-1 $296. Scenarios: bear $150 (25%), base $267 (50%), bull $342 (25%, lowered from $370 to an 18x multiple). The ladder is a three-lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.25/0.20/0.18) plus a 5% wide tail component: mean ~$263, median ~$262, P(up) ~61%, P(<$166) ~17%. The ladder sits slightly above the blended fair value because the FCF leg is a deliberately rate-harsh cross-check. Research limits: Kalshi returned 429 and Polymarket's December page was the 2025 market, so Fed odds rest on the Kalshi search snapshot and the DeFi Rate aggregator; the Moody's capex note returned 403. memo.title: NVDA: long a decade-low 19.5x NTM multiple; target $268.93, stop $174.61, add only if late-Oct capex guides clear our base case
memo.call_reason: Published 12-month target $268.93 is 12.6% above the $238.90 close, P(gain) is 0.63 and the conviction rubric reads medium, but the expected excess return barely covers ~38% volatility, so the position stays small and staged.
memo.one_liner: NVDA trades at ~19.5x NTM EPS, a decade low and below AVGO/TSM, with FY28 guided to ~+70% revenue; even after assuming the multiple compresses to 16x we get a $263 research target (12m) and a $268.93 target. The risk is a 2027-28 hyperscaler capex digestion, so we hold 1 share and add only if the Oct 27-30 capex guides and the ~Nov 17-18 Q3 FY27 print confirm demand.

thesis.point: The valuation already prices heavy de-rating: the stock is flat in a year only at ~13.9x Oct-2027 NTM EPS.
thesis.evidence: $238.90 is ~19.5x NTM consensus EPS of $12.00-12.25 (Q3 FY27-Q2 FY28; stockanalysis fwd P/E 19.34x), vs AVGO 20.49x and TSM 20.65x. Consistent Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $17.1 means a flat year needs ~13.9x, a further ~29% de-rating. All five agents assume compression to 16-17x and still reach research targets (12m) of $250-296.

thesis.point: Earnings visibility through FY28 is unusually high and supply-constrained.
thesis.evidence: Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), Data Center $89.0B (+117%), non-GAAP GM 75.0%. The Q3 guide is $108.0B ±2% at 74.0% GM. Management's preliminary FY28 view is ~+70% revenue at 72-73% GM after a 71-72% Q4 trough. $279B of supply and capacity commitments back the ramp.

thesis.point: Customer capex keeps being revised up, and backlogs fund the 2027 ramp.
thesis.evidence: Big-4 2026 capex guides rose from ~$655B to $732.5B during the year, and none was cut. 2027 Big-4 consensus is $934.5B (IO Fund) to $1,029B (S&P), against our base case of $1,080B. Backlogs: MSFT commercial RPO $678B, Google Cloud $513.9B, AWS $496B. Year-ahead consensus drift was +25% to +62% in each of 2024-26.

memo.variant_view: There is no strong variant view against the options market. Our $268.93 target and 0.63 P(gain) sit close to the options-only distribution (target $263.75, P(gain) 0.61, 15th percentile $173.36). Against the sell side we are more cautious: the 50-analyst median target is $315 (range $210-515, Strong Buy), ~17% above ours. The gap is the multiple, not EPS: we assume 16x on Oct-2027 NTM EPS because FY29 growth should slow to low-to-mid teens. Our customer-capex work adds a second gap. At base capture, base-case 2027 capex implies FY28 revenue of ~$647B, 6% below the $687B consensus, and NVIDIA's supply cap (~$700-750B) limits FY28 upside. So we are below the Street on both multiple and FY28 revenue, and in line with options. [sources 9, 11, 12]

valuation.methods: Supervisor research target (12m) $263 is a blend of two legs. P/E (60%): consistent Oct-2027 NTM EPS (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) of $17.1 = H2 FY28 consensus $8.90 + H1 FY29 ~$8.5 (FY29 +13-15%, ~2% memory-cost haircut), x 16x = $274. FCF yield (40%): $17.1 x 23.9B shares x 72% conversion = $12.3/share at a 5.0% yield = $246, + ~$1 net cash = $247. Agent research targets (12m) $250/$255/$260/$270/$296 (median $260). agent_4 is high on 17x and a 4.5% yield. 16x is ~22% below the AVGO/TSM 20.57x anchor. The published target $268.93 is the median of the blended options-plus-agents distribution. Thesis break $160.

The two biggest finds: the retiree health plan's prior-service credit, which props up adjusted EPS, mostly runs out in 2027 (10-K Note 14 balance; other income ~2,290 in 2026 -> ~1,189 in 2027 and ~551 after), and SpaceX's mobile entry now takes about 0.44M / 0.67M of AT&T's 2028-29 phone adds on top of the post-SpaceX 6.1x multiple Kilian kept. Revenue per phone is built from price actions (flat without one, a half-size back-book rise in 2028), Internet Air adds fade, home internet ARPU -2% in 2027, and AC EBITDA follows a 0.84 flow-through on service revenue from a Q4 2026 base of 11,696. The result sits moderately below management and consensus: 2028 adjusted EPS $2.78 vs the $2.82 floor, FCF $17.6B / $19.8B vs $19B+ / $21B+, consolidated EBITDA 3.0% under consensus in 2028 (50,995 vs 52,561). One card is open for Kilian (management's 20%+ home internet revenue pace, +7.8%), plus two smaller option sets (industry phone pool after 2026, home internet quarter shape).

tax_assumptions._ignore_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: ignore taxes for now (he has money set aside for the liability). Set false to use the tax facts below.
tax_assumptions._future_note: Combined rate you'd expect on today's embedded gains when you'd otherwise sell (15% federal + ~6% state once working). Drives the sell cost and the gain-harvest suggestion.
tax_assumptions._tax_note: Kilian 2026-09-28: taxable account; ~$20,000 internship wages in 2026 plus realized gains; claimed as a dependent by a parent living in CA; full-time student under 24 living in CT. Assumed (not confirmed): domicile stays CA (a student living away at school keeps the parents' domicile, FTB Pub 1031), CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode so CT does not tax investment income; kiddie tax applies (earned income not more than half of his support). Federal 2026 figures from IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; CA brackets are 2025 (FTB Tax News Oct 2025), 2026's not published yet.
tax_assumptions._other_unearned_note: Dividends etc. this year (rough: GOOGL + META dividends). Counts toward the kiddie-tax threshold.
tax_assumptions._kiddie_note: Unearned income above $2,700 (2 x $1,350, Rev. Proc. 2025-32) is taxed at the parent's rate, federal (Form 8615) and CA (FTB 3800). Applies to a full-time student 19-23 whose earned income is not more than half of his own support.
tax_assumptions._parent_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: parent in NYC, 37% federal bracket. Parent's NY/NYC rates do not apply to Kilian's gains (no NY kiddie tax under Form 8615).
tax_assumptions._flat_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 22:04Z: the parent claiming him lives in New York City (37% federal bracket; NY 9.65%, NYC 3.876% at the parent's income). Federal kiddie tax (Form 8615): unearned income above kiddie_threshold ($2,700) at the parent's federal rates, short-term 37%, long-term 20% (the 37% bracket is above the 20% LTCG start, Rev. Proc. 2025-32); up to the threshold at Kilian's own federal rates, 10% short-term (wages $20k less the $16,100 dependent standard deduction leave ~$3.9k taxable, inside the 10% band to $12,400) and 0% long-term. New York has no kiddie tax when Form 8615 is used: the child's investment income is reported on the child's own NY return and taxed at the child's own rates (NYS IT-201-I, 'Does your child have investment income over $2,700?'). So NY and NYC tax every gain at Kilian's own marginal rates: NY 5.40% ($13,900-80,650) + NYC 3.762% ($12,000-25,000), single, 2026 schedules (NYS IT-2105-I 2026); NY dependent standard deduction $3,100. Assumed: Kilian is domiciled at the parent's NYC home (a dependent student keeps the parents' domicile) and his CT dorm is not a permanent place of abode. NIIT dropped (Kilian 2026-10-21 00:48Z 'yes you may drop it'; it was kept per his 2026-10-01 20:32Z ask): Form 8960 applies it on the child's own MAGI over $200,000 (single), which his income does not reach. Short-term = 37% + 9.162% = 46.162%; long-term = 20% + 9.162% = 29.162%; own rates under the threshold 19.162% / 9.162%. Was CA (41.3% / 28.1% / 14% / 2%) until 2026-10-20. Net losses offset gains; up to $3,000 deducts at the own short-term rate. Bracket mode (mode 'brackets') still holds the CA schedule and is not updated.
tax_assumptions._short_term_all_note: Kilian 2026-10-28 card 'Assume short-term on all' (thread 'Fix AMAT target vs sell mismatch'): every holding is assumed sold within the year at the short-term rate, so a trim only pays the same tax H years sooner; band per year = q tau (1 - (1+d)^-H) / H + spread / T. Overrides lot_aware_horizon; false restores it.
tax_assumptions._lot_aware_note: Kilian 2026-10-20 card 'Lot-aware' (Assumption audit thread): a short-term lot's trim band compares selling now with holding it to its one-year date and selling long-term: band per year = q (tau_now - flat_long_term_rate (1+d)^-X) / X, X = years until the oldest (FIFO) lot turns long-term (floor 1 day), plus spread / T. Long-term lots keep the T-year rule (years_until_you_would_otherwise_sell, future_rate_on_deferred_gains, Claude defaults 2026-09-28). false restores the T-year rule for every lot.

agents.reasoning: Round 2 (supervisor fact-checks plus a direct read of the AT&T Q3 call transcript, 10-Q R63/R17 and FCC auction notes). Evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adj. EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adj. EPS $0.65, FCF ~$5.0B; 379k postpaid phone adds, churn 0.92%; postpaid phone ARPU +4% from new/refreshed plans and back-book pricing with promotions unchanged (call); fiber ARPU -4% with Q4 similar and "relatively stable ARPU" over 2026-28 (CFO). GAAP EPS $0.12-0.13 carries a $2.6B Mexico impairment and an ~$800M separation charge whose cash lands mainly in 2027. Guides: 2026 EPS ~$2.40, AC EBITDA mid-to-high single digits, consolidated EBITDA 5%+ in 2028, FCF $18B+/$19B+/$21B+, capital investment $22-23B in 2027-28, $24B+ buybacks, 2.5x leverage in 2029. Price moves: Oct 9 (-10.8%) = SpaceX buying Grain's 800 MHz licences (no ex-dividend effect: ex-date Oct 12); Oct 21 (-6.4%) = results day (phone-add miss, capex/working-capital framing), a small earnings-path change; Oct 23 (-8.0%) = Bloomberg report of SpaceX seeking 80,000+ sites, a multiple effect. What changed from round 1: Forged Fiber stake $4,058M x 0.9 (R63) instead of $2.58B; separation cash no longer double-counted in net debt (horizon $147.9B, now linked to driver FCF); wireless ARPU +1.5%/+0.8% (was +0.6%/+0.4%); fiber ARPU -1.0%/+0.5% (was +0.7%/+1.6%); AC EBITDA +6.0%/+6.0%; interest +$0.1B; upper C-band -$5B x 0.35; P/E 8.1x and FCF yield 12.3% held at today's levels (were 8.5x / 12.0%); EPS, FCF/share and horizon net debt are now computed from the drivers through driver_build.set. Peers: Kilian's 12 incumbents on CY2027E, after leases: EV/EBITDA median 5.52x (5.98x ex-DT), P/E 10.55x; AT&T 5.78x / 7.98x on that basis. Result: research target (12m) $23.88 (EV/EBITDA $23.43, P/E $24.37, FCF $24.26); bear $15.15 (price war, 5.3x), bull $29.23 (6.9x). Guidance record: EPS first guides met or beaten 3 of 3 (median +2.7%), FCF floors 3 of 3 (+3.75%); we sit just below the 2027 FCF floor ($18.9B) and the 2028 EBITDA 5% (4.7% ex-Mexico) because of Legacy and fiber ARPU, and above the 2028 EPS floor on buybacks. Ladder: 60% the scenario mixture (lognormal, 15% within-scenario vol), 40% a neutral 28%-vol distribution centred near spot, because the October de-rating came from SpaceX headlines that may continue and momentum is negative; median ~$22.8, P(>= $21) 0.605. All value legs are driver-linked; the dividend and peer-median cross-checks carry zero weight.

Facts fixed: fiber stake now +4,058 x 0.9 as an equity adjustment (R63; round 1 had ~$1.7B in net debt); net debt at the horizon re-derived at 145.4B (Q4 FCF ~6B, 68% of FY27 FCF by Oct-23, three dividends, ~$7B/yr buybacks, NCI/preferred, Mexico x0.9); FCF per share on horizon shares (6,385M); postpaid phone base on reported year-end counts (73.4815M); home-internet FY26 average time-weighted for the Lumen subscribers (14.06M), which lowers fiber ARPU to the -4% the company reports. Model deepened: a sixth driver, the AC EBITDA margin, now sets segment EBIT, and the P/E and FCF legs read EPS and FCF computed from the drivers; Legacy is a plain run-off segment (driven revenue 81%). Industry follow-ups (8 searches/fetches): Verizon steering to the top of its 750k-1M phone-add guide with no free phones (TIKR), Comcast blaming fiber's $30-40 gig pricing for its losses, SpaceX's own plan of rooftop small cells rather than macro towers (Wireless Estimator), and FCC rules forcing the upper C-band auction to close by July 2027 (Light Reading). agents.reasoning: 1) Facts: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $0.65; GAAP $0.12 carries a $2.56bn non-cash impairment on held-for-sale Mexico and an ~$800M separation charge (cash mainly 2027). Outlook: 2026 EPS ~$2.40, capital investment $22-23bn for 2027-28, FCF $18B+/$19B+/$21B+, Q4 FCF ~$6B, 2026 cash taxes ~$750M under OBBBA (call). 2) October drops: Oct 9 (-10.8%) = Grain's sale of its 800 MHz licences to SpaceX (no ex-dividend that day: record/ex-date was Oct 12; round-1 error corrected); Oct 21 (-6.4%) = results day, slower adds (379k) and fiber ARPU -4%; Oct 23 (-8.0%) = Bloomberg report of SpaceX talks for 80,000+ sites. All three move the multiple more than 2026-27 earnings; I keep the de-rating. 3) Revisions from the supervisor: preferred $2,950M now deducted (-$0.46/share); the Composite Fiber 37 / Lumen Mass Markets stake added at book 4,058 less 15% (+$0.54); Auction 115 re-timed with its 2027-04-27 start and sized from Auction 107 (-$6bn x 0.5 = -$0.47, vs -$0.31 round 1); FY2025 segment base replaced with the Ex.99.4 recast; peers replaced with the 12-incumbent CY2027E after-lease set (5.52x / 10.55x). 4) Driver build: postpaid phones 74.9/76.2/77.2M avg, wireless revenue per phone +1.7/+1.5/+0.8% (from +1.0/+0.8; supervisor +1.75%: I stay lower because the CFO says growth comes from adds, not pricing), connections 15.4/18.4/21.1M, blended broadband ARPU -8.4/-2.5/-1.5% (CFO: fiber ARPU stable), AC EBITDA +6.4/+6.0/+5.5% (inside the mid-to-high single-digit guide; supervisor +6.25/+6.0), capital investment 23.4/22.8/22.8bn -> adjusted EBITDA 48.2/49.5/50.7bn (consensus 2027 49.75bn, 2028 52.0bn), EPS 2.41/2.63/2.86 (Zacks 2.38/2.54/2.86), FCF ~18.1/18.7/20.4bn (below the 19+/21+ floors; record of three floors met carries 45% weight). Net debt at the horizon $145.4bn, 6,400M shares. 5) Valuation: EV/EBITDA 6.1x = $22.20 (w 0.5), P/E 8.2x = $23.19 (w 0.35), FCF yield 12% = $24.07 (w 0.15) -> research target (12m) $22.83 (+9.1%, plus $1.11 dividends); round 1 $22.44. The P/E EPS and FCF/share are stated (not driver-linked inside the engine). 6) Base rates (my lane) and how they enter: T's 12-month price change after similar setups (down >12% over a year, within 6% of the 52-week low; weekly samples since 1991 ex-WarnerMedia spin) median -5.4%, 37% positive (n=103 overlapping, few independent episodes); pooled six telcos (n=578) median +5.4%, p10 -28%, p90 +41%. They enter the ladder as a separate component, not through the scenarios: a lognormal with median $21.13 (20.93 x exp(0.4 x ln 0.946 + 0.6 x ln 1.054) = 20.93 x 1.0094) and sigma 0.262 (pooled p10/p90 spread / 2.563), weight 0.30. The other 0.70 is the engine's scenario mix (bear $15.39 / base $22.83 / bull $28.69 at 25/50/25%, within-scenario vol 0.14). Result: median ~$22.20, below the research target; P(>=21) 0.582, P(>=25) 0.315, P(>=16.74) 0.812. Event odds: Polymarket SpaceX US carrier 13% by mid-2027 / 34.5% by end-2027 (thin, ~$15k, cross-check only); Fed cut by March 2027 14%. 7) Sources: ~half are company filings/releases and the brief-mandated peer pages (data); the discretionary ones are mostly in lane (Yahoo base-rate studies, Polymarket, FRED, FCC/Auction 107/AWS-3 history, new-entrant precedents). Research limited to 8 follow-up queries this round.

supervisor.summary: AT&T's research target (12m) is $22.99, the engine value of a driver set rebuilt from evidence on 2026-11-10 and corrected in the citation-gate fix (was $23.15 before the rebuild). The two biggest finds: the retiree health plan's prior-service credit, which props up adjusted EPS, mostly runs out in 2027 (10-K Note 14 balance; other income ~2,290 in 2026 -> ~1,189 in 2027 and ~551 after), and SpaceX's mobile entry now takes about 0.44M / 0.67M of AT&T's 2028-29 phone adds on top of the post-SpaceX 6.1x multiple Kilian kept. Revenue per phone is built from price actions (flat without one, a half-size back-book rise in 2028), Internet Air adds fade, home internet ARPU -2% in 2027, and AC EBITDA follows a 0.84 flow-through on service revenue from a Q4 2026 base of 11,696. The result sits moderately below management and consensus: 2028 adjusted EPS $2.78 vs the $2.82 floor, FCF $17.6B / $19.8B vs $19B+ / $21B+, consolidated EBITDA 3.0% under consensus in 2028 (50,995 vs 52,561). One card is open for Kilian (management's 20%+ home internet revenue pace, +7.8%), plus two smaller option sets (industry phone pool after 2026, home internet quarter shape).

memo.title: AT&T (T) Long: SpaceX de-rating priced in, cash path intact - target $22.65, research target (12m) $23.16 plus a 5.3% yield
memo.call_reason: The published target ($22.65) is above the $20.93 price and conviction is medium (rubric), with a 5.3% dividend on top and a stop at $16.54 that sits on the $16.5 thesis-break level.
memo.one_liner: AT&T lost ~16% in October on SpaceX headlines (Grain 800 MHz licences, a reported 80,000-site push) while Q3 beat and 2026 EPS was raised; our horizon multiples keep that de-rating and still value the shares at a research target (12m) of $23.16 (+10.6%) on the earnings path alone. We buy 167 shares at or below the page's Entry below (~$21.60), ahead of this week's peer prints and the Oct-29 FCC vote, stop $16.54, take-profit $27.52.

thesis.point: Earnings power is rising, not falling: EPS growth from lower D&A and ~5% a year of buybacks carries value even at today's de-rated multiples.
thesis.evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adjusted EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adjusted EPS $0.65; 2026 EPS guide raised to ~$2.40, mainly on lower depreciation from held-for-sale accounting for Mexico. Our driver build gives adjusted EPS $2.66 (2027) and $2.91 (2028) vs Zacks consensus $2.54 / $2.86; at 8.3x (AT&T's own NTM P/E today) the P/E leg alone is $24.01.

thesis.point: The October drawdown is a multiple event, and we keep it in the target rather than betting on a rebound.
thesis.evidence: Closes fell 24.87 -> 22.18 (-10.8%) on Oct-9 (SpaceX buys Grain's 800 MHz licences), 23.42 -> 21.91 (-6.4%) on results day Oct-21, and 22.74 -> 20.93 (-8.0%) on Oct-23 (Bloomberg: SpaceX seeks 80,000+ sites). The horizon EV/EBITDA stays at the post-news 6.1x (~$2.8/sh of de-rating retained; 6.1x = 5.69x on the peer basis vs an 11-incumbent median of 5.98x ex-DT). SpaceX targets next-generation service by end-2027, so most fourth-carrier cash-flow damage falls after our 2027-10-23 horizon.

thesis.point: Cash returns and asset sales put a floor under the equity.
thesis.evidence: $0.2775 quarterly dividend (5.3% yield at $20.93), $24B+ of buybacks guided for 2026-28, Mexico sale for ~$2.0B cash at closing (Q1 2027) and a 50% fiber JV stake carried at $4,058M (taken at x0.9 = +$3.65B). At the $16.5 thesis break the stock would yield 6.7% and ~15% FCF-to-common at ~5.2x EBITDA on the peer basis, a level consistent only with a broken cash path.

memo.variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Sell-side (24 analysts, Buy) has a median target of $28.00 (mean $27.80, range $20-34), roughly 21% above our research target (12m) of $23.16: we keep the post-SpaceX 6.1x EV/EBITDA and model FCF of $18.5B / $19.9B for 2027-28, below both management's $19B+ / $21B+ floors and consensus ($19.24B / $20.97B), because Legacy EBITDA turns negative after 2027 and wireless ARPU growth fades to +0.75% in 2028. The options market is more bearish than we are: its standalone 12-month median is $21.35 with P(gain) 52.7%, vs our published 60.2%. Our variant view is therefore narrow and specific: EPS (above consensus on lower D&A and buybacks) carries value at a de-rated multiple, so we do not need the SpaceX fear to fade to make money; a move back toward the pre-October ~6.8x would add ~$2.8/sh on top. This is not a large mispricing call; most of the expected return is the dividend plus a modest earnings-path gain.

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $23.16 = model-engine base horizon value (23.1576) of the supervisor's reconciled driver set (wireless and fiber subs x ARPU, Advanced Connectivity margin, capital investment ~$23.4B/22.8B/22.7B): EV/EBITDA 6.1x on NTM EBITDA ~$50.4B = $22.55 (weight 0.5), P/E 8.3x on driver-linked NTM EPS $2.86 = $24.01 (0.35), 12.3% FCF yield on $2.82/share = $23.19 (0.15); net debt at horizon $144.3B, NCI $18.0B, preferred $2.95B, fiber stake +$3.65B, expected upper C-band spend -$2.0B (-$5B x 0.4), 6,387M shares. No DCF leg (not in the DCF policy for this sector). The five forecasters' values span $22.24-24.39. The published target $22.65 is the median of the final distribution, which blends the options market (weight 0.67, median $21.35) with the research ladder (0.33); expected value $23.42 (+11.9%), P(gain) 60.2%. Bear values $15.15-16.68 (price war, cable-like ~5.2-5.3x), bull values $27.51-29.23 (re-rating toward ~6.8-7.0x).

risks.risk: SpaceX becomes a priced, national fourth carrier (Grain 800 MHz + EchoStar spectrum + leased terrestrial sites); supervisor probability 0.35 over 2028-2031, and the market can price it well before then (bear values $15.15-16.68).
risks.signpost: A signed site-lease deal for tens of thousands of towers; FCC approval of the Grain licences with terrestrial rights; a US price list for Starlink Mobile; Polymarket odds of a US carrier by end-2027 rising from 34.5% (thin market).

risks.risk: Free cash flow misses the floors and buybacks slow: we already sit below management ($18.5B vs $19B+ in 2027), and the 2025 tax-law cash benefit runs off after 2027.
risks.signpost: Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B or capital investment above $23B; buyback pace below the ~$24B+ 2026-28 plan.

risks.risk: Wireless price competition: Verizon is taking share (406k Q3 phone adds, guide raised to 1.1-1.2M) while AT&T adds slowed to 379k; fiber ARPU is already -4% y/y.

risks.risk: Balance sheet: 3.13x leverage with the 2.5x target pushed to 2029, a Fitch BBB+ Negative Outlook, $9.5B of debt due within a year and possible ~$5B upper C-band spend.
risks.signpost: A Fitch downgrade, AT&T qualifying to bid heavily in Auction 115, refinancing at materially higher coupons.
