agents.method_text: Blend of 9.5x NTM adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA at the horizon ($8.41B, after Cogentrix and the Meta PPAs) = $171.0 (70%) and a DCF at 9.15% WACC with 2.0% Gordon growth = $140.9 (30%). Equals the standard engine's base horizon value of $161.96.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA at horizon $8,414M x 9.5x = EV $79.9B - net debt $20.9B - preferred/NCI $2.49B + Cogentrix tax NPV $0.63B = $57.2B / 334.3M shares (incl. ~1.1M SBC shares) = $171.0

inputs_detail.derivation: Estimate derived from reported 10-Q lines at 2026-06-30 (no net-debt figure is reported): long-term debt due currently 1,876 + long-term debt less current 17,719 = 19,595, less cash and cash equivalents 435 = 19,160. Excludes AR financing 300, the forward repurchase obligation 613 and restricted cash 46. [citation gate 2026-10-14]

Estimate: sum of two reported XBRL facts at 2026-06-30 (10-Q accn 0001692819-26-000019): PreferredStockValue 2,476 + MinorityInterest 12 = 2,488. Treated as debt-like claims ahead of common equity. [citation gate 2026-10-14]

19,160 + Cogentrix cash 2,300 and assumed debt 1,500 (src 5) - ~15 months of Adj. FCFbG at ~4,300/yr = ~5,400 (2026 guidance midpoint, src 3) + growth spend ex-Cogentrix ~1,500 (part of the $4.5-5B 2026-27 growth allocation, src 4) + buybacks ~1,250 (remaining ~$1.2B authorization by YE2027, src 3) + common and preferred dividends ~580 = ~20,900. The $1.5B junior subordinated notes (src 9) raise debt and cash equally, so they are left out of the net figure. The notes' prospectus says proceeds may redeem the 8.0% Series A and 7.0% Series B preferred after their Oct/Dec 2026 resets (src 25); if so, ~$1.5B shifts from preferred to net debt and total claims ahead of common (~$23.4B) are unchanged, so the bridge keeps that total.

335.6M outstanding (2026-08-03, F103) - ~7.4M repurchased with ~$1.15B at ~$155 (remaining authorization, src 3) + 5.0M Cogentrix consideration shares (src 5) + ~1.1M stock-comp shares (SBC dilution: TTM SBC $134M (F46) / ~$150 x 1.25 years) = 335.6 - 7.42 + 5.0 + 1.12 = ~334.3M (corrected from 334.6M, an addition error, citation gate 2026-10-14). SBC is counted here, not in FCFF.

inputs_detail.input: NTM adjusted EBITDA at horizon (Q4-2027 to Q3-2028)
inputs_detail.derivation: Model rows: FY2027 8,104 (= low end of the $7.4-7.8B 2027 midpoint opportunity, which management said is trending to the lower end, src 4, plus ~$700M from Cogentrix (~$4.0B / 7.25x = ~$550M, Vistra release src 6) and the Meta PPA premium (src 4, 7)); FY2028 8,497 (+~5%: full Meta operating delivery by YE2027 (src 7), PJM capacity flat at $325 vs $333 (src 8), ERCOT soft, only ~72% hedged (src 3)). NTM = 0.21 x FY2027 + 0.79 x FY2028. Pre-SBC, the same basis as peer consensus adjusted EBITDA (src 27). The thin FMP consensus for the window (~$9,370M, 1-4 analysts, src 19) is not used; this sits ~10% below it.

Peer NTM EV/EBITDA median 10.6x, range 8.9x (NRG) to 11.8x (CEG), on consensus adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA (src 20, 27). VST trades ~9.5-9.8x today: EV ~$72.7B (152.2 x 335.6M = $51.1B + $19.16B net debt + $2.49B preferred/NCI) on ~$7.4-7.6B NTM EBITDA before the deals. 9.5x is about where it trades now, ~1.1x below the median, between NRG and TLN. The discount reflects merchant ERCOT exposure (2028 only ~72% hedged, src 3), the undecided PJM 2030/31+ design with a consumer push to cap existing generation (src 23, 24), and the gas-heavy fleet vs CEG. No premium is claimed.
$700M = '~$0.7 billion of net present value of expected tax benefits' in Vistra's release (src 6) x 0.9 closing probability = $630M (~$1.9/share).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY2026-29 FCFF (adj. EBITDA ~37% of revenue, capex 14%->9.5%, 20% tax, SBC as dilution not cost) discounted at 9.15%; Gordon terminal growth 2.0% after FY2029 (~86% of DCF value); exit-9.0x cross-check $153

Capex FY2025 2,752 (F57), TTM 2,866 (F60, ~15% of TTM revenue, includes growth projects); declines as the Permian peakers and other growth projects are completed.

FY2025 SBC 113 / revenue 17,586 = 0.64% (F43, F3); TTM 134 (F46) on ~19,600 FY2026 revenue = ~0.7%. Under sbc_treatment 'dilution' it is carried as ~1.1M extra shares by the horizon instead of a cash cost.

Cost of equity 10.71% = 10-yr UST 5.21% on 2026-10-13 (src 21) + beta ~1.1 (judgment for a merchant IPP) x 5% ERP. Pre-tax marginal debt cost 6.5%: TTM average 5.8% (interest 1,132 / debt 19,595, F81/F98) is below today's marginal cost, shown by the 7.000%/7.250% junior notes issued 2026-09-24 (src 9); x (1 - 20%) = 5.2%. Preferred ~7.5% (8.0%/7.0% series, src 25). Weights on EV $72.7B: 70.3% equity, 26.4% net debt, 3.4% preferred -> 9.16%, used as 9.15% (round 1: 8.5% with 5.24% rf and 5.8% debt cost).

agents.reasoning: Round 2. Cause of the drop, now pinned: September CPI was released 2026-10-14 08:30 ET at +0.6% m/m and +3.7% y/y (core +0.3% m/m, +2.6% y/y; energy +5.2% m/m) (BLS, src 22), with the 10-yr at 5.21% (src 21). VST closed -6.5% with CEG -5.5%, TLN -6.2% and NRG -5.9%, against SPY -1.1% and XLU -0.3% (src 18). Vistra filed nothing (latest 8-K 2026-10-05, src 11). The move is sector-wide, a rates/AI-power factor sell-off, not company news, so fair value does not move because of it. Changes from round 1 (supervisor feedback, verified at the primaries): (1) SBC is now counted once, as dilution, on pre-SBC EBITDA like the peers; round 1 deducted it in FCFF and also added the shares. (2) WACC is 8.5% -> 9.15%, on rf 5.21% and a 6.5% marginal debt cost (new 7.0-7.25% junior notes). (3) The DCF terminal is now Gordon 2.0% instead of a 9.0x exit, which was equivalent to ~2.35% growth and reused peer multiples: DCF $155 -> $141. (4) The P/E leg is dropped. (5) The Cogentrix tax NPV now cites Vistra's own release (src 6), not The Fly. (6) The AI-capex low case (src 26) is added to the bear case and long-dated risks. New in-lane evidence: the 424B5 shows the junior notes may fund redemption of the 8.0%/7.0% preferred (claims-neutral, src 25); a 2026-07-15 PJM workshop presentation by the Ohio Energy Group proposes keeping the cap and floor on existing generation beyond 2029/30 (src 24). PJM's own answer leaves the 2030/31+ path to after its end-2026 stakeholder review (src 23), so I raise the PJM-cap probability from 0.35 to 0.4. Valuation: 9.5x NTM adjusted EBITDA of $8.41B = $171.0 (70%), DCF $140.9 (30%), fair value $162.0 (round 1 $165.0). Scenarios $110.6 / $162.0 / $212.4 at 25/50/25, lognormal mix with 30% within-scenario vol (~39% total), so the 12-month median is ~$158.7, ~4% above spot. Thesis break moves from $120 to $115, ~8.0x pro forma 2027 EBITDA. The sell-side median target of $210 (src 19) is near my bull case and was not used. About 8 follow-up searches/fetches; www.sec.gov pages were read via WebFetch, data.sec.gov JSON directly.

methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA at 2027-10-14 $8.41B x 9.5x = EV $79.9B; - net debt incl. preferred $22.96B - minorities $0.01B + Cogentrix tax NPV $0.63B = equity $57.6B / 334.6M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Low end of the $7.4-7.8B midpoint opportunity ($7.4B; CFO: 'trending towards the lower end') + ~$0.7B Cogentrix and Meta PPAs ('add roughly $700 million ... absent any other impacts') = $8.1B. Round-1 $0.2B ERCOT haircut removed: it had no sourced curve figure behind it. $8.1B / $21,272M = 38.1% less 10.9% D&A = 27.2%.

No management 2028 figure. $8.1B + full-year Cogentrix (~$4.0B net price / 7.25x = ~$0.55B/yr, so ~+$0.1B for the part of 2027 before close) + Meta uprate PPAs and Comanche Peak AWS load from end-2027 (+~$0.3B) - ERCOT: 2028 only ~72% hedged with forwards 'meaningfully lower' and 2028/29 PJM capacity at $325 vs $333 (2027/28) (-~$0.0-0.1B) = ~$8.5B (+5%). Replaces round-1 $9.0B, which leaned on a 1-2 analyst FMP consensus.

inputs_detail.input: Net debt incl. preferred at horizon 2027-10-14
inputs_detail.derivation: 19,160 - 2,160 (H2-2026 Adj. FCFbG: half of guidance midpoint $4,325M) - 3,840 (2027 FCFbG ~$4,860M = 8.1B x 60% conversion (2026 guide 4,325/7,200), x 0.79 yr to Oct-14) + 3,800 (Cogentrix $2.3B cash + $1.5B assumed debt, fully counted) + 1,800 (other growth: $4.5-5B 2026-27 program less $2.3B Cogentrix cash = $2.2-2.7B, ~75% spent after 2026-06-30 by the horizon, incl. memo.title: VST: small, staged long into the Q4 catalyst cluster; ~9% to a $150.54 target on 2027 EBITDA roll-forward, not re-rating
memo.call_reason: Target $150.54 is above the $138.02 price with medium conviction and no special situation, but the edge is thin (P(gain) 0.57) so size is capped at 5 shares and entry is staged around the Q3 guide.
memo.one_liner: At ~9x pro-forma 2027 EBITDA of ~$8.15B, VST is priced for the contracted nuclear/PJM book with no credit for ERCOT recovery; formalizing the 2027 guide and a cap-level PJM auction should carry it to ~$151 research target (12m). The Street at ~$219 is paying for an 11x re-rating we don't underwrite, and the stock sits only ~$33 above the $105 thesis-break level at 45-49% vol, so we buy small and add on the print.

thesis.point: 2027 EBITDA of ~$8.1B is largely locked: the low end of the $7.4-7.8B opportunity plus ~$0.7B from Cogentrix and the Meta premium, with 2027 ~94% hedged.
thesis.evidence: CFO on the Q2 call: 2027 'trending towards the lower end' and Cogentrix plus Meta 'add roughly $700 million'; hedges 100%/94%/72% for 2026/27/28. EIA's September STEO held 2027 ERCOT generation at ~527 TWh and raised 2027 ERCOT North to $34.30/MWh, so the August load-growth cut did not extend.

thesis.point: At ~$138 the stock trades at ~9x forward EBITDA, only ~1.8 turns above the 7.25x plain gas-fleet M&A mark, so the contracted nuclear (Meta 2.6 GW PJM, AWS 1.2 GW Comanche Peak) and PJM capacity at the $325 cap are cheaply valued.
thesis.evidence: Cogentrix bought at 7.25x 2027 EBITDA; PJM 2028/29 BRA cleared at the $325/MW-day cap (10,924 MW for Vistra) and the collar extends through 2029/30; ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred and ~337M diluted shares give ~$105 at 7.2x.

thesis.point: Insiders and the balance sheet are supportive: the CEO bought in the open market after the drawdown, and the preferred is being refinanced into cheaper junior notes rather than equity.
thesis.evidence: CEO Form 4 purchases Aug 24 and Aug 31-Sep 1, 2026; $1.5B 7.000%/7.250% junior subordinated notes (Sep 24) fund redemption of the 8.0% Series A and 7.0% Series B preferred at their resets. Offset: the CFO sold 20,000 shares at $151.03 under a 10b5-1 plan.

memo.variant_view: Versus the Street we are the bear: our $150.54 target is ~31% below the weighted analyst median of $218.97 (17 analysts, low $169 Mizuho, high $298). Street targets need ~11x EBITDA or ~$8.5B+ 2028 EBITDA, which requires ERCOT forwards to turn and new hyperscaler deals; with ~28% of 2028 unhedged into a curve still falling in late September, we don't underwrite that. Versus the options market we are only modestly more constructive: the market-implied median is $141.57 with P(gain) 0.52, against our $150.54 and 0.57; our edge is the belief that the Q3 guide formalizes ~$8.1B and that the EIA Texas load cut is already in the price. That is a small variant view, not a big one, and it is why the position is small.

valuation.methods: Supervisor blend, same as the five agents' mean ($150.9; range $145-156): (1) 9.0x ~$8.15B forward EBITDA = ~$73.4B EV, less ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred, over 337M diluted shares = ~$148 (50% weight); (2) ~$13.9/share FCF before growth at a 9% yield = ~$154 (30%); (3) ~13.5x ~$11.1 forward EPS = ~$150 (20%). Blend ~$151. The published 12-month target ($150.54) is the median of the combined options-market and agent distribution; expected value is $170.65 because of the fat right tail (q75 $206.50). Each 0.25x on the multiple is ~$6/share; the $8.1B vs $8.25B EBITDA dispute is ~$2.7/share.

catalysts.event: PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement bid window (~6.8 GW shortfall, cost cap $555/MW-day)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Clearing prices near the cap would confirm scarcity value in PJM and data-center-paid capacity; a weak outcome or political cost-allocation fights would pressure the PJM story ahead of the BRA.
catalysts.watch: Procured MW vs the 6,831 MW target and the clearing price relative to $325 and $555/MW-day.

catalysts.event: Series A preferred first reset / earliest redemption date (8.0% rate ends); Series B reset in Dec 2026
catalysts.why_it_moves: Redemption funded by the Sep-24 junior notes removes the reset risk and lowers the fixed charge; mostly housekeeping.
catalysts.watch: Redemption notice/8-K for the full $1.0B Series A; no equity issuance.

catalysts.event: FOMC rate decision
catalysts.why_it_moves: IPP multiples compressed as the 10-year approached 5%; VST is a levered, high-multiple name, so a hawkish surprise hits it harder than the market.
catalysts.watch: Hike vs hold and the 10-year's reaction; a move back above 5% is a multiple headwind.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings and formal 2026/2027 guidance update including Cogentrix and Meta
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the event that formalizes (or breaks) the ~$8.1B 2027 base the whole valuation sits on, and gives the first read on 2028 hedging.
catalysts.watch: 2027 guide at or above ~$8.1B incl. ~$0.7B Cogentrix+Meta (below $7.4B low end is a thesis hit); 2028 hedge % and price; buyback pace; any new hyperscaler contract; whether guidance waits for the Cogentrix close.

catalysts.event: Cogentrix acquisition close (FERC approved Aug 2026; HSR and customary conditions outstanding)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Unlocks ~5.5 GW of gas and the Cogentrix share of the $0.7B EBITDA add; a slip delays the formal 2027 guide.
catalysts.watch: Closing 8-K; 5M shares issued to seller; $1.5B assumed debt.

catalysts.event: ERCOT files the Batch Zero Eligibility Verification and Community Impact Review reports (governor-ordered data-center audit); energization of new 75 MW+ loads paused until then
catalysts.why_it_moves: Determines how much of the Texas large-load queue is real, which drives the ERCOT load-growth narrative and the 2028 forward curve on VST's open volume.
catalysts.watch: Share of the ~128 GW studied load that survives; restart date for Batch Zero and energizations; any new PUCT rules for large loads or co-location.

catalysts.date: mid-Dec 2026 (agents cite 2026-12-15 close; PJM confirms December)
catalysts.event: PJM 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction under the $325 cap / $175 floor collar
catalysts.why_it_moves: Sets East capacity revenue for June 2029 onward; a fourth cap-level clear supports the out-year story (adds nothing to NTM EBITDA).
catalysts.watch: Clearing price vs $325 cap; reserve shortfall; any talk of extending the collar or more affordability intervention.

catalysts.event: Texas 90th Legislature convenes (session through late May 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Bills on large-load limits, data-center cost allocation or co-location could cut the ERCOT demand story that underpins 2028+ pricing.
catalysts.watch: Filed bills on large-load interconnection, curtailment or co-location; committee hearings in Feb-Mar.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results: first 2028 outlook and updated hedge levels (~72% hedged as of Aug 2026)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The 2028 view tells us whether EBITDA grows past 2027 or rolls over as the open ~28% re-hedges at weaker ERCOT forwards; it sets the NTM base at our horizon.
catalysts.watch: 2028 opportunity range vs ~$8.1-8.2B; hedge % and realized prices; buyback authorization.

risks.risk: The Q3 guide lands below the $7.4B low end plus $0.7B, or the 2028 view comes in below 2027, as the ~28% open 2028 volume is re-hedged into weak ERCOT forwards.
risks.signpost: ERCOT 2027/2028 forwards keep falling week over week (they were down ~2.0%/1.7% in the week of Sep 21); management language shifts from 'lower end' to 'below the range'; continued downward EPS revisions.

risks.risk: Texas large-load demand disappoints: the Dec 10 audit culls much of the queue and the 2027 legislature restricts data-center interconnection, cementing the ~$30-34/MWh ERCOT curve.
risks.signpost: Audit reports show a large share of the 128 GW studied load ineligible; Batch Zero restart pushed to late 2027; another EIA STEO cut to Texas load growth (August already cut 2027 to 6% from 14%).

risks.risk: Sector de-rating: IPPs trade as a group on AI-power sentiment and rates; a hyperscaler capex pause or a 10-year above 5% compresses the multiple toward the 7.25x gas-fleet mark (~$105).
risks.signpost: CEG/NRG/TLN falling together with VST; hyperscaler capex guidance cuts; 10-year sustained above 5%.

agents.method_text: Rate-base EPS build (avg rate base x 53.5% equity x earned ROE ~8.2-8.3% in 2027-28 after the MN freeze and PSCo test-year lag, less HoldCo drag, over the forward-equity share path) gives NTM EPS $4.77 at the horizon; 17.2x (XEL's current 0.91x relative to the 18.85x peer median) less $0.12/sh Smokehouse = $81.92 weighted 0.8, blended with a driver DCF at 5.94% WACC / 3.5% g and $50.1B horizon net debt = $55.31 weighted 0.2 -> $76.6.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at 2027-10-20 $4.77 (rate-base build: FY27 $4.455, FY28 $4.844) x 17.2x, less $0.12/sh probability-weighted Smokehouse Creek excess loss

inputs_detail.derivation: Company 'Strong rate base growth' slide on the $60B base plan; incremental rate base assumed +$3B avg 2028, +$6B 2029, +$9B 2030.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If the incremental $10B slips, 2028-30 EPS ~2-3% lower (about -$2/sh at 17.2x).

inputs_detail.derivation: Authorised operating-company capital structures from rate-case orders (not the consolidated ~41% in the deck's credit metrics): PSCo 54.5% (CPUC decision, 8-K 2026-08-19), NSPM 52.5% and SPS 54.7% (Q2 2026 deck rate-case pages), NSPW 52.5% (PSCW decision for 2026 rates, Q4 2025 release); 2025 rate-base mix PSCo 43% / NSPM 35% / SPS 16% / NSPW 6% (deck): 0.43x54.5 + 0.35x52.5 + 0.16x54.7 + 0.06x52.5 = 53.71% (53.93% with PSCo at 55%). The earlier '~53.5%' did not compute; this build ran at 53.5% with an earned ROE calibrated to 2026 guidance on that same ratio, so only the product enters EPS: on 53.71% the same OpCo earnings imply ROEs x 0.996 (e.g. 8.28% -> 8.25% in 2027) and EPS and value are unchanged.

Round-1 path (8.37/8.36/8.28/8.40/8.75%) was calibrated to guidance on the TTM June-2026 OpCo ongoing ROE of 8.43% (NSPM 9.59%, NSPW 10.31%, PSCo 7.22%, SPS 8.51% [3]). Two filings since then add lag: (a) NSPM proposes a base-rate freeze for 2027-28, offset by accelerated battery-storage ITC recognition, with trackers continuing [20]; NSPM is ~35% of rate base, and I assume the ITC offset covers most but not all of the 2027-28 revenue requirement: NSPM -10bp (2027) and -20bp (2028) -> -0.035pp and -0.070pp on the total; (b) the CPUC set PSCo rates on a 13-month average 2025 historical test year, $157M vs $356M requested, ROE 9.3%, equity 54.5% [21]; PSCo is ~43% of rate base and growing fast, so -10bp on PSCo -> -0.043pp in 2027-28. 2027: 8.36 - 0.035 - 0.043 = 8.28%; 2028: 8.28 - 0.070 - 0.043 = 8.17%; 2029 8.40 - 0.10 = 8.30% and 2030 8.75 - 0.05 = 8.70% as the freeze ends and the new MN case resets. Check FY2027: avg RB $71.5B x 53.5% x 8.282% = $3,168M - HoldCo $250M = $2,918M / 655M = $4.455.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If the ITC acceleration fully offsets the MN freeze (the company proposed it and reaffirmed nothing yet for 2027), FY28 EPS is ~$4.88 and value ~+$0.5/sh; if the MPUC rejects the plan and the early-2027 rate case brings interim rates, similar; if the offset is small, NSPM -40bp in 2028 -> FY28 ~$4.80 (-$0.6/sh).

inputs_detail.derivation: Xcel Energy Inc. & Other was -$0.10/sh YTD 2026 (~-$130M annualised); HoldCo debt 22-24% of total debt and rising with $22.8B incremental debt 2026-30, ~$+100M/yr after-tax interest at ~5.5% coupons (2026 HoldCo junior sub 5.75%). Gate check: the stated basis does not compute to ~$100M a year: 22-24% (HoldCo share) x $22.8B incremental debt over 2026-30 = ~$5.2B, i.e. ~$1.05B a year x ~5.5% x (1-21%) = ~$46M a year, a path of -$150M / -$196M / -$241M / -$287M / -$332M. The extra ~$54M a year in this agent's path (-$250M / -$350M / -$420M / -$480M) is its own assumption with no stated derivation (e.g. repricing of existing HoldCo debt would need to be shown).
inputs_detail.variant_view: On the stated-basis path (-$196M 2027, -$241M 2028) EPS would be FY2027 $4.54, FY2028 $5.00, NTM $4.91: P/E leg $84.33 (+$2.41) and blend ~$80.2 (engine re-run in the gate fix, not adopted: agent view). The reconciled set uses its own drag (-$125M/-$190M/-$260M), which is reconciled to the reported segment.

inputs_detail.derivation: OpCo earnings (avg rate base $61.0/71.5/84.5/94.0/101.0B incl. incremental x 53.5% x earned ROE above) - HoldCo drag $150/250/350/420/480M, / avg diluted shares 628/655/690/710/730M: FY26 $2,581.5M/628 = $4.11; FY27 $2,918.1M/655 = $4.455; FY28 $3,342.1M/690 = $4.844; FY29 $3,754.1M/710 = $5.287; FY30 $4,221.0M/730 = $5.782. FY26 sits at the reaffirmed $4.04-4.16 guide midpoint [21]; FY26-28 growth ~8.6%/yr. vs consensus: FY26 $4.12 (-0.2%), FY27 $4.54 (-1.9%) [15]; the gap is the MN freeze and PSCo test-year lag, which consensus may not fully carry.

If FY28 reaches round 1's $4.92 (management's 9%+ path), NTM = 0.197 x $4.455 + 0.803 x $4.92 = $4.83: +$1.0/sh at 17.2x.

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer median NTM P/E 18.85x [17]; XEL today 76.68 / NTM consensus $4.46 (0.197 x 4.1212 + 0.803 x 4.5403) = 17.2x, i.e. 0.91x the table median but 0.93x the consistent-basis peer median 18.45x (supervisor re-weighting of peers.json to XEL's Oct-2026 window 0.197 FY2026 / 0.803 FY2027; the peers.md table median 18.85x mixes NTM windows: WEC, CMS, AEE, ES use 0.504/0.496 and LNT, PPL, CNP, EVRG 0.753/0.247). Round 1 used 17.5x (narrowing to a 7% discount) with no dated catalyst for the narrowing; I now hold today's relative: the discount's causes persist through the horizon (un-legislated CO wildfire liability, Texas AG suit, $7B equity plus ~40% equity on incremental capex, PSCo/NSPM lag [2,3,20,21]) and higher-for-longer long rates are a risk to the whole group, while ~8.6% EPS growth vs the 7.8% peer median argues against widening it. agents.reasoning: Round 2. Start: $76.68, -5.5% over a year, after wildfire litigation (Smokehouse Creek, Texas AG), MN/CO regulatory pressure (CPUC $157M of $356M on a historical test year; NSPM 2027-28 freeze filing) and a 10y that peaked at 5.31% on Oct 5 and closed at 5.12% on Oct 20. I do not keep the supervisor's suggestion to hold $4.88: the corrected share count has to flow through. NTM EPS at the horizon $4.70 (supervisor $4.79; consensus-equivalent ~$4.87); (4) net debt at the horizon $48.5B from front-loaded capex; (5) the Abernathy-Anthropic link is dropped: the TeraWulf 8-K names Fluidstack with a Google backstop and pass-through power. Valuation: 17.3x x $4.70 - $0.23 = $81.1 (weight 0.8) and DCF $50.8 (0.2) = $75.03, 2% under spot, plus a ~3% dividend: fairly priced to slightly rich. Alternative-lane signals: organised data-centre opposition (Data Center Watch; MN AG on Pine Island; metro moratoria) is a real approval risk that Anthropic's S-1 risk factor confirms; Polymarket prices no 2026 Fed cut; prediction markets put the Anthropic IPO mostly in late Nov-Dec 2026. Kilian's liquidity-drain question: Tunguz estimates $432-576B of liquidity for the three mega-IPOs at normal floats, but expected 3-8% floats mean the actual raise is far smaller (reports say up to $100B for Anthropic) and S&P 500 inclusion is delayed; index funds would fund it by selling mega-cap tech, not utilities. XEL's holders (income and utility funds) overlap little with IPO buyers, and the S-1 does not change XEL's earnings; the only channel is the AI-power trade (XEL partly trades as a data-centre load name). So I expect at most a short, flow-driven dip. Plan: if XEL drops to ~$70-72 on IPO flow or rates with the Oct-29 plan intact (no extra equity beyond ~40% of incremental capex, 2027 guide >= ~$4.40), that is a buying opportunity: $70 is 14.9x NTM $4.70, ~7% under my value plus ~3% dividend (~10% 12-month total return). Do not buy a dip that comes with a wildfire or regulatory headline; below $64 is the thesis break: re-underwrite. Ladder: lognormal mixture around the engine scenarios ($59.7/$75.0/$88.3 at 25/50/25, 12% within-scenario vol, 4% weight on a 35%-vol tail), shifted half-way to spot because the price itself beats fair-value blends as a 12-month forecast; median ~$75.6, P(>=77) 0.46. Research: 9 web queries this round; Reddit/X gave nothing usable; no current Polymarket volume for the 2027-deadline Anthropic market was found. Lane: 18 of 32 sources are alternative; the rest are filings, data and the brief's WSJ fact, which the brief allows for basic facts.

agents.reasoning: Round 2. Base rates first: XEL's 12-month price returns 2005-2026 (250 overlapping windows, Twelve Data) had median +8.3%, s.d. 12.6%, 26% negative, 10% below -10%, built mostly in a falling-rate era; now the 10Y is 5.12%, the Fed hiked on 9/16 and Polymarket prices another hike (Dec +25bp 77.5%; 10Y >= 5.5% before 2027 25%). Supervisor findings I accepted: horizon shares 650M was below the 651.9M floor (only the 27.3M 2025 forwards settle before the horizon; 10-Q) -> 658M; NEE dropped, ES back in (median 18.85x unchanged); the NSPM 2027-28 freeze filing and CPUC 13-month historical test year (both 8-Ks, re-read) -> 2027/2028 EPS $4.45/$4.95 (from $4.55/$5.06), NTM $4.85 (from $4.95); my 7.0% WACC + 14x exit was inconsistent -> Gordon 3.5% on a steady-state FY2030 at one WACC. Where I keep my own view: 2028 EPS sits ~1.6% above the strict 9% path ($4.87) because XEL has met guidance 21 years running, the guide is '9%+' and roll-forwards usually add capex; net debt $50.2B (vs $48.5B) because I keep $1.0B of 2027 incremental capex and TTM CFO after dividends is only $3.4B. WACC: I measured XEL's 2-year weekly beta to SPY at 0.21 (Blume 0.47) and moved the cost of equity from 8.4% to 7.7%, WACC 6.4% (supervisor 6.0%). Once the DCF is consistent it says the business is worth about book (~$45/share) at a CAPM cost of capital; the market pays ~2x book on a lower implied cost of equity (reverse DCF 5.8%). Blend: 0.8 x $83.30 + 0.2 x $44.92 = $75.62 fair value (from $79.11), with the P/E leg essentially unchanged ($83.66 -> $83.30: lower EPS, higher 17.2x multiple once I dropped an unsupported round-down). Ladder: I do not centre on the engine median ($75.2): over 12 months prices follow the forward P/E (playbook, Liu-Nissim-Thomas) and the P/E leg sits on the +8% base rate, while the book-value DCF is an anchor the market has not converged to. So the ladder is ~50/50 the engine's scenario mix (bear $63.05 / base $75.62 / bull $86.57, 25/50/25, 11% within-scenario vol) and a P/E-led lognormal (median $82, 16.5% vol), with a fatter left tail for wildfire jump risk (Feb-2024 single-day -8%): median ~$77.5, P(>= $69) 0.76, P(>= $92) 0.15. Kilian's question (does the Anthropic IPO drain liquidity from XEL, and is a dip a buy?): the nearest base rate is the SpaceX IPO, week of 9 June 2026: selling hit the Magnificent Seven (all fell; Moneyfarm) while XEL (+0.2%) and XLU (+0.4%) rose that week and +1.6%/+2.2% through June (Twelve Data). The IPO literature's asset-supply channel (Packer and Spiegel, BIS WP 888) hurts stocks that co-move with the new issue; XEL's correlation to SPY is 0.16 and its holders are income/utility funds. So I expect no meaningful drain on XEL; if one comes through a broad risk-off or a lock-up wave, with the 10Y and fundamentals unchanged, below ~$70 (14.4x my horizon NTM EPS, under the late-September washout of 15.4x NTM) is a buying opportunity; below the $63 thesis break, re-underwrite instead. The bigger near-term drivers are the 10Y and the Oct-29 capital/equity plan. On the WSJ S-1: ~$450B of mostly noncancelable cloud commitments (Google $111B plus a >$160B TPU lease) is a general demand positive through Google, Xcel's largest data-centre counterparty (Pine Island ESA; Abernathy backstop). No named source ties Anthropic load to an Xcel site: Abernathy (SPS) is a Fluidstack campus with a Google backstop and power 100% passed through (TeraWulf 8-K); Anthropic's reported Texas sites are in Central Texas. The S-1's 'more organized and coordinated' opposition risk is already visible in XEL's states (MN AG on the Google ESA, NSPM freeze, CPUC test year). AI-tenant counterparty risk falls first on tariff terms (MN 15-year minimum and exit fees; CO proposed 80% minimum bill and deposits); SPS TX/NM tariffs are not yet filed, which is the gap where shareholders carry it. Research limited to public pages; X/Twitter not used.

supervisor.confidence_reason: My checks confirmed the inputs that move the price (NTM EPS ~$4.78 matches the agents' mean; 17.2x is XEL's current multiple) and found two method errors: the DCF tax-shield double count (lowers agents 2-4's DCF leg) and the mixed-basis peer median (no value effect). Fair value moves only ~2% below the mean (75.2 vs 76.5), on a 0.2-weight leg whose level is very sensitive to the WACC, so the ladder shift is small and not clearly a better forecast.

supervisor.summary: XEL is fairly priced: the reconciled rate-base build (NTM EPS $4.78 at 17.2x) and a consistent driver DCF give $75.2 (ex-dividend) vs $76.68, a ~2% total return plus a ~3.1% yield. The forecasters agree on the business; my checks fixed a DCF error (interest tax shield counted twice by agents 2-4) and a mixed-basis peer median (XEL trades at 0.93x a consistent 18.45x, not 0.91x). The swing factors are the 10y, the Oct-29 equity plan and MN/CO regulation, not the Anthropic IPO, which has no verified link to Xcel's territory. A rates-neutral dip toward $70 is buyable; $63 is the thesis break.

invested_cash.meaning: dollar gain on stocks (price, dividends, realized and unrealized) / average dollars in stocks; SPY and equal weight = the same dollars on the same days in them instead

live_book.spy_basis: price plus distributions reinvested on the ex-date (dividends.json); no adjusted closes in the data
live_book.dividends_missing_note: names not in dividends.json are treated as paying nothing
live_book.note: 31 trading days of returns cannot show skill: daily stock returns swing by about 1-2%, so a gap of a few percent over a few weeks is well within luck. rough_se treats days as independent; read the gaps as what happened, not as evidence, until there are many months. Whole book: time-weighted, cash at the T-bill, vs fully invested SPY and equal weight. Invested cash: dollar-weighted on the stock sleeve, vs the same dollars in SPY and equal weight.
